sentences.zh: 廖紀，字時陳，東光人。

translations.literal: Liao Ji, styled Shichen, was a native of Dongguang.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Ji, courtesy name Shichen, came from Dongguang.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年進士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 授考功主事，屢遷文選郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director in the Bureau of Appointments and was repeatedly promoted to Department Director of the Bureau of Selection.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a director in the Bureau of Appointments and rose repeatedly until he became department director of the Bureau of Selection.

sentences.zh: 正德中，歷工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign he served as Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhengde emperor he served as right vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 提督易州山廠，羨金無所私。

translations.literal: Supervising the Yizhou mountain depots, he kept none of the surplus funds for himself.
translations.idiomatic: As supervisor of the Yizhou mountain depots he never kept surplus revenue for himself.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left and Right Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left and right vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，拜南京吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Shizong acceded, he was appointed Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing emperor came to the throne, Liao was appointed minister of personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 調兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of War to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Ministry of War to assist in military planning.

sentences.zh: 被論解職。

translations.literal: He was impeached and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Impeachment drove him from office.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，「大禮」議既定，吏部尚書楊旦赴召，道劾張璁、桂萼。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing, after the Great Rites controversy was settled, Minister of Personnel Yang Dan, summoned on the road, impeached Zhang Cong and Gui E.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 3, once the Great Rites debate was settled, Yang Dan, minister of personnel, was summoned to court and on the way impeached Zhang Cong and Gui E.

sentences.zh: 璁、萼之黨陳洸遂劾旦而薦紀。

translations.literal: Chen Guang, a partisan of Cong and E, thereupon impeached Dan and recommended Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guang, an ally of Cong and Gui E, then impeached Yang Dan and recommended Liao Ji in his place.

sentences.zh: 帝罷旦，以紀代之。

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed Dan and replaced him with Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor removed Yang Dan and appointed Liao Ji minister in his stead.

sentences.zh: 紀疏辭，言：「臣年已七十，精力不如喬宇，聰明不如楊旦。

translations.literal: Ji memorialized to decline, saying, "Your servant is already seventy; my vigor is not equal to Qiao Yu's, nor my acuity to Yang Dan's.
translations.idiomatic: Liao memorialized to decline, writing, "I am already seventy; I lack Qiao Yu's energy and Yang Dan's sharpness.

sentences.zh: 」時宇、旦方為帝所惡，不許。

translations.literal: " At that time Yu and Dan were just then detested by the emperor, and he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu and Dan were then out of favor with the emperor, and he would not allow Liao to step down.

sentences.zh: 光祿署丞何淵請建世室，祀興獻帝，下廷議。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments He Yuan asked to build a Shishi hall to sacrifice to Emperor Xingxian, and the matter was sent down for court debate.
translations.idiomatic: He Yuan, an assistant director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments, petitioned to build a Shishi hall to honor the Jiajing emperor's father, and the court was ordered to debate it.

sentences.zh: 紀等執不可，帝弗從。

translations.literal: Ji and others held that it could not be done; the emperor did not follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Liao and his colleagues insisted it must not be done, but the emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 紀力爭曰：「淵所言，幹君臣之分，亂昭穆之倫，蔑祖宗之制，臣謹昧死請罷勿議。

translations.literal: Ji strove in argument, saying, "What Yuan proposes violates the distinction between ruler and minister, disorders the order of senior and junior lines, and scorns the institutions of the ancestors; your servant respectfully risks death in asking that it be abandoned and not debated.
translations.idiomatic: Liao pressed the point: "Yuan's proposal trespasses on the bond between ruler and subject, scrambles the order of the ancestral lines, and scorns the institutions of the forefathers. I beg Your Majesty, at the risk of my life, to drop the plan and forbid further debate.

sentences.zh: 」不納。

translations.literal: " It was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not accept his plea.

sentences.zh: 會廷臣多諍者，議竟寢。

translations.literal: As it happened, many court officials remonstrated, and the proposal was ultimately shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Because many officials remonstrated, the proposal was eventually dropped.

sentences.zh: 已，條奏三事。

translations.literal: Thereafter he memorialized in separate items on three matters.
translations.idiomatic: Later he submitted a memorial setting forth three proposals.

sentences.zh: 其末言人材當惜，謂：「正德之季，宗社幾危。

translations.literal: The last spoke of cherishing talent, saying, "At the end of Zhengde the altars of state were nearly lost.
translations.idiomatic: The last urged the emperor to value talent, arguing, "At the close of the Zhengde reign the dynasty nearly perished.

sentences.zh: 議者但知平定逆藩之功，而不知保護京師之力。

translations.literal: Those who debate know only the merit of pacifying the rebellious princedom and do not know the strength that protected the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators praise only the suppression of the rebel prince and forget those who held Beijing secure.

sentences.zh: 自陛下繼統，老成接踵去，新進連茹登，以出位喜事為賢，以淩分犯禮為貴。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, seasoned men have left one after another while newcomers mount in succession like gourds on a vine; stepping beyond one's place to court affairs is deemed worthy, and overstepping ranks to violate ritual is held honorable.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession, seasoned ministers have departed in succession while newcomers rise like gourds on a vine; meddling beyond one's station is praised as talent, and trampling ritual hierarchy is treated as distinction.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下於昔年致仕大臣，念其保護之勛，量行召用。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty, regarding the great ministers who retired in former years, will recall their merit in protecting the state and summon them as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to recall the retired elders who once shielded the throne and summon them back as their merits warrant.

sentences.zh: 其他降職、除名、遣戍者，使得以才自效。

translations.literal: As for others demoted, struck from the rolls, or sent to frontier garrison, let them be enabled to offer their talents in service.
translations.idiomatic: Let those demoted, struck from office, or exiled to the frontier also be allowed to serve according to their abilities.

sentences.zh: 」帝但納其正士風、重守令二事而已。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted only his two points on rectifying the scholar-official ethos and valuing prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor adopted only his proposals to reform official conduct and to strengthen local prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 三邊總督楊一清召還內閣，璁等欲起王瓊，紀推彭澤、王守仁，帝不允。

translations.literal: Yang Yiqing, supreme commander of the Three Frontiers, was recalled to the Grand Secretariat; Cong and others wished to raise Wang Qiong, but Ji recommended Peng Ze and Wang Shouren, and the emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yiqing, supreme commander of the Three Frontiers, was recalled to the Grand Secretariat, Cong's faction wanted Wang Qiong restored, but Liao recommended Peng Ze and Wang Shouren; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 復以鄧廷璋、王憲名上，竟用憲。

translations.literal: He again submitted the names of Deng Tingzhang and Wang Xian, and in the end Xian was used.
translations.idiomatic: He then nominated Deng Tingzhang and Wang Xian, and Wang Xian was appointed.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，御史張袞、喻茂堅、朱實昌以世廟禮成，請宥議禮得罪諸臣，璁、萼亦以為請，章俱下吏部。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Censors Zhang Gun, Yu Maojian, and Zhu Shichang, because the rites of the Imperial Ancestral Temple were completed, asked pardon for the officials punished in the Rites controversy; Cong and E also so petitioned, and all memorials were sent down to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jiajing 5, after the ancestral temple rites were completed, censors Zhang Gun, Yu Maojian, and Zhu Shichang petitioned to pardon officials punished in the Rites debate; Cong and Gui E joined the plea, and all memorials went to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 紀等列上四十七人，卒報罷。

translations.literal: Ji and others listed forty-seven men and submitted them; in the end the response was denial.
translations.idiomatic: Liao and his colleagues submitted a list of forty-seven names, but the emperor ultimately refused.

sentences.zh: 御史魏有本以劾郭勛、救馬永謫官，給事中沈漢等論救，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Censor Wei Youben was demoted for impeaching Guo Xun and pleading for Ma Yong; Supervising Secretaries Shen Han and others argued in his defense, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wei Youben was demoted for impeaching Guo Xun and defending Ma Yong; supervising secretaries led by Shen Han pleaded for him, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 紀從容為言，且薦永及楊銳。

translations.literal: Ji spoke on his behalf at ease and also recommended Yong and Yang Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Liao spoke calmly on Wei's behalf and also recommended Ma Yong and Yang Rui.

sentences.zh: 帝納之，有本得無謫。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it, and Youben was not demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and Wei Youben was spared demotion.

sentences.zh: 紀在南都，持議與璁合，坐是劾罷。

translations.literal: When Ji was in the Southern Capital his views accorded with Cong's, and for this he was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: While at Nanjing Liao had sided with Zhang Cong on policy and was impeached and removed for it.

sentences.zh: 璁輩欲引助己，遂首六卿。

translations.literal: Cong's faction wished to draw him to aid themselves, and he thereupon headed the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's faction wanted his help and installed him at the head of the six ministries.

sentences.zh: 而紀顧數與抵牾，璁輩亦不喜。

translations.literal: Yet Ji repeatedly clashed with them instead, and Cong's faction also disliked him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liao often opposed them, and they in turn grew displeased with him.

sentences.zh: 年老稱病乞歸，許之去。

translations.literal: Old in years, he pleaded illness and asked to retire; he was permitted to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Citing age and illness, he asked to retire and was allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 初，《獻皇實錄》成，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Veritable Records of the Xian Emperor were completed, he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of the Xian emperor were completed, he had been made grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 至是進少保，賜敕乘傳，夫廩視故事有加。

translations.literal: At this time he was advanced to Junior Guardian, granted an edict to travel by relay post, and his allotment of bearers and grain exceeded precedent.
translations.idiomatic: On his retirement he was promoted to junior guardian, granted imperial transport by relay, and given a larger allowance of bearers and grain than usual.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太傅，謚僖靖。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor, with the posthumous title Xijing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made grand tutor with the posthumous title Xijing.

sentences.zh: 王時中，字道夫，黃縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Shizhong, styled Daofu, was a native of Huang County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhong, courtesy name Daofu, came from Huang County.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年進士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 授鄢陵知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yanling.

sentences.zh: 嘗出郊，旋風擁馬首。

translations.literal: Once when he went out to the suburbs, a whirlwind enveloped his horse's head.
translations.idiomatic: Once on an outing beyond the city walls a whirlwind swirled about his horse's head.

sentences.zh: 時中曰：「冤氣也。

translations.literal: Shizhong said, "This is the breath of injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong said, "That is the breath of a wronged soul.

sentences.zh: 」跡得屍眢井，乃婦與所私者殺之，遂伏辜。

translations.literal: " Tracing it, he found a corpse in a ruined well; a woman and her lover had killed the victim, and they then suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Following the sign he found a corpse in an abandoned well; a woman and her lover had murdered the man, and both were punished.

sentences.zh: 召拜御史，督察畿輔馬政。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Censor to supervise horse administration in the metropolitan region.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as censor supervising horse administration in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 正德初，請革近畿皇莊，不報。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he asked to abolish imperial estates near the capital; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he petitioned to abolish imperial estates near the capital, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書馬文升致仕，時望屬劉大夏、閔珪。

translations.literal: When Minister of Personnel Ma Wensheng retired, public expectation rested on Liu Daxia and Min Gui.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Ma Wensheng retired, public opinion favored Liu Daxia or Min Gui as his successor.

sentences.zh: 時中詆珪和媚，大夏昏耄。

translations.literal: Shizhong denounced Gui as compliant and fawning and Daxia as senile.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong attacked Min Gui as obsequious and Liu Daxia as senile.

sentences.zh: 兩人各求退，焦芳遂得之，眾鹹咎時中。

translations.literal: Both men each sought to withdraw, and Jiao Fang thereupon obtained the post; all blamed Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Both men withdrew from consideration, Jiao Fang won the appointment, and many blamed Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 出按宣、大，逮系武職貪汙者百余，為東廠太監邱聚所奏。

translations.literal: Sent out to investigate Xuanfu and Datong, he arrested and bound more than a hundred military officers for corruption; he was impeached by the eunuch Qiu Ju of the Eastern Depot.
translations.idiomatic: On inspection tour in Xuanfu and Datong he arrested more than a hundred corrupt military officers, provoking an impeachment from Qiu Ju of the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾捕時中下詔獄，荷重枷於都察院門。

translations.literal: Liu Jin seized Shizhong and put him in the imperial prison, bearing a heavy cangue at the gate of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin had him thrown into the imperial prison and made to wear a heavy cangue at the Censorate gate.

sentences.zh: 時中病甚，其妻往省，遇都御史劉宇，哭且詬。

translations.literal: Shizhong was gravely ill; his wife went to visit him, met Censor-in-Chief Liu Yu, and wept while reviling him.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened his wife visited him, met Censor-in-Chief Liu Yu, and wept while cursing him.

sentences.zh: 宇不得已言於瑾，釋之，謫戍鐵嶺衛。

translations.literal: Yu had no choice but to speak to Jin, who released him and banished him to garrison duty at Tieling Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yu finally appealed to Jin, who released Wang and banished him to garrison duty at Tieling Guard.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起四川副使，遷湖廣按察使。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, he was raised to Vice Commissioner of Sichuan and transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's execution he was restored as vice commissioner of Sichuan and later became surveillance commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十二年以右僉都御史巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，召為右副都御史。

translations.literal: When Shizong acceded, he was summoned as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing emperor came to the throne, Wang was summoned as right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 父喪除，起故官。

translations.literal: After mourning for his father ended, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 會上章聖太后尊號，時中言本生二字不當去。

translations.literal: When the honorific title of the Zhangsheng Empress Dowager was conferred, Shizhong said the two characters "born of the original line" ought not to be removed.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager's honorific title was issued, he argued that the words "born of the original line" should not be dropped.

sentences.zh: 及上冊寶，百官陪列不至者九人，時中與焉。

translations.literal: When the imperial seal and regalia were presented, nine officials among those in attendance did not arrive, and Shizhong was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial regalia were presented, nine officials failed to attend the ceremony, Wang among them.

sentences.zh: 帝責對狀，已而貰之。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him and required an explanation in person, but afterward pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to answer for his absence but eventually pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部左侍郎，代李鉞為尚書。

translations.literal: He served as Left Vice Minister of War and replaced Li Yue as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left vice minister of war and succeeded Li Yue as minister.

sentences.zh: 中官黃英等多所陳請，時中皆執不可。

translations.literal: The palace eunuch Huang Ying and others made many petitions; Shizhong on each held that they could not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs such as Huang Ying petitioned for favors, he consistently refused.

sentences.zh: 敘薊州平盜功，濫及通州守備鄢祐，為言官李鳴鶴等所劾。

translations.literal: In recounting merit for pacifying bandits in Jizhou, he indiscriminately included Tongzhou garrison commander Yan You and was impeached by remonstrating officials led by Li Minghe.
translations.idiomatic: In reporting merit for suppressing bandits at Jizhou he improperly included Tongzhou garrison commander Yan You and was impeached by censors led by Li Minghe.

sentences.zh: 時中乞休，且詆言者。

translations.literal: Shizhong asked to retire and also reviled the remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: Wang asked to retire and insulted his critics.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉世揚等言時中不當逞忿箝言官，帝乃切責時中，令歸聽勘。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Liu Shiyang and others said Shizhong ought not vent anger to muzzle remonstrating officials; the emperor thereupon sharply rebuked Shizhong and ordered him home pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries led by Liu Shiyang argued that Wang must not silence censors in anger; the emperor sharply rebuked him and ordered him home pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年四月起復為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year of Jiajing he was recalled and restored as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Jiajing 10 he was recalled as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 御史郭希愈請重兵部侍郎之選，以邊臣有才者兩人分掌邊方、內地軍務。

translations.literal: Censor Guo Xiyu asked to strengthen the selection of vice ministers of war, with two talented frontier officials respectively to manage military affairs on the border and in the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Guo Xiyu proposed elevating the selection of vice ministers of war so that two capable frontier officials could divide border and interior military affairs.

sentences.zh: 吏部議從之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel deliberated and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 時中言非祖宗臨時遣將意，帝遂從其議。

translations.literal: Shizhong said this was not the ancestral intent in dispatching generals ad hoc; the emperor thereupon followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: Wang argued that this departed from the ancestral practice of dispatching generals ad hoc, and the emperor accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 帝欲用王憲於兵部，乃調時中刑部尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to use Wang Xian in the Ministry of War, and so transferred Shizhong to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted Wang Xian at the Ministry of War and transferred Wang Shizhong to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 坐論御史馮恩獄，落職閑住。

translations.literal: For discussing the case of Censor Feng En in prison, he was dismissed and lived in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his handling of censor Feng En's imprisonment he was dismissed and lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 始，恩疏詆時中，及是以寬恩得罪，時稱為長者。

translations.literal: At first En had memorialized to denounce Shizhong; now he offended by leniency toward En, and contemporaries called him a man of forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Feng En had once memorialized against him, yet Wang lost office for being lenient toward En; contemporaries praised his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 久之，遇赦，復官致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time, on encountering an amnesty, his office was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, after an amnesty, his rank was restored and he retired.

sentences.zh: 周期雍，字汝和，江西寧州人。

translations.literal: Zhou Qiyong, styled Ruhe, was a native of Ningzhou in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qiyong, courtesy name Ruhe, came from Ningzhou in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 授南京御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾既誅，為瑾斥者悉起，而給事中李光翰、任惠、徐蕃、牧相、徐暹、趙士賢，御史貢安甫、史良佐、曹閔、王弘、葛浩、姚學禮、張鳴鳳、王良臣、徐鈺、趙佑、楊璋、朱廷聲、劉玉，部郎李夢陽、王綸、孫磐等，以兼劾群閹未得錄。

translations.literal: After Liu Jin was executed, all whom Jin had dismissed were restored, but Supervising Secretaries Li Guanghan, Ren Hui, Xu Fan, Mu Xiang, Xu Xian, and Zhao Shixian, Censors Gong Anfu, Shi Liangzuo, Cao Min, Wang Hong, Ge Hao, Yao Xueli, Zhang Mingfeng, Wang Liangchen, Xu Yu, Zhao You, Yang Zhang, Zhu Tingsheng, and Liu Yu, and department directors Li Mengyang, Wang Lun, Sun Pan, and others, because they had jointly impeached the eunuch clique, were not recorded for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jin's execution most of his victims were restored, but supervising secretaries Li Guanghan, Ren Hui, Xu Fan, Mu Xiang, Xu Xian, and Zhao Shixian, censors Gong Anfu, Shi Liangzuo, Cao Min, Wang Hong, Ge Hao, Yao Xueli, Zhang Mingfeng, Wang Liangchen, Xu Yu, Zhao You, Yang Zhang, Zhu Tingsheng, and Liu Yu, and department directors Li Mengyang, Wang Lun, Sun Pan, and others who had jointly impeached the eunuch clique were left off the restoration list.

sentences.zh: 期雍偕同官王佩力請，皆召用。

translations.literal: Qiyong together with his colleague Wang Pei strongly petitioned, and all were summoned and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyong and his colleague Wang Pei pressed the case vigorously, and all were summoned back to office.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書王敞附瑾進，期雍請斥之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Wang Chang had advanced through attachment to Jin; Qiyong asked that he be expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Chang had risen through Jin's patronage, and Qiyong petitioned for his removal.

sentences.zh: 焦芳、劉宇猶在列，而劉大夏、韓文、楊守隨、林瀚、張敷華未雪，期雍皆極論。

translations.literal: Jiao Fang and Liu Yu were still in office, while Liu Daxia, Han Wen, Yang Shousui, Lin Han, and Zhang Fuhua had not been vindicated; Qiyong argued forcefully on all these points.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Fang and Liu Yu still held office while Liu Daxia, Han Wen, Yang Shousui, Lin Han, and Zhang Fuhua remained unredeemed; Qiyong pressed each case forcefully.

sentences.zh: 陳金討江西賊，縱苗殺掠，期雍發其狀。

translations.literal: Chen Jin campaigned against bandits in Jiangxi and allowed the Miao to kill and plunder; Qiyong exposed the facts.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Jin campaigned against Jiangxi bandits he let the Miao kill and plunder; Qiyong exposed the abuse.

sentences.zh: 尋清軍廣東，劾鎮守武定侯郭勛，金與勛皆被責。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, inspecting troops in Guangdong, he impeached the garrison commander Marquis Guo Xun of Wuding; both Jin and Xun were rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting troops in Guangdong he impeached garrison commander Marquis Guo Xun of Wuding, and both Chen Jin and Xun were rebuked.

sentences.zh: 出為福建僉事。

translations.literal: He went out as Assistant Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 宸濠反，簡銳卒赴討。

translations.literal: When Prince Chenghao rebelled, he selected crack troops and hurried to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chenghao rebelled he raised crack troops and marched to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 會賊平乃還。

translations.literal: Only when the rebels were pacified did he return.
translations.idiomatic: He returned only after the rebellion was crushed.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，為浙江參議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he served as Assistant Administrator of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he became assistant administrator of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 討平溫、處礦盜，予一子官。

translations.literal: He pacified bandits in the Wenzhou and Chuzhou mines and was granted an office for one son.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed bandits in the Wenzhou and Chuzhou mines and was granted an office for one son.

sentences.zh: 再遷湖廣按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 九年擢右僉都御史，巡撫順天。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 薊州、密雲關堡數十，以避寇警移入內地，關外益無備，期雍悉修復之。

translations.literal: Several dozen passes and forts at Jizhou and Miyun had been moved inland to avoid bandit alarms, leaving the outer frontier ever more undefended; Qiyong restored them all.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of passes and forts at Jizhou and Miyun had been moved inland to escape bandit raids, leaving the frontier undefended; Qiyong restored them all.

sentences.zh: 數列上便宜。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized on measures of immediate benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted practical proposals for reform.

sentences.zh: 入為大理卿，歷刑部左、右侍郎，右都御史，拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He entered office as President of the Court of Judicial Review, served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Justice and Right Censor-in-Chief, and was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He became president of the Court of Judicial Review, rose through left and right vice minister of justice to right censor-in-chief, and was appointed minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 大計京官，言官劾期雍納賄。

translations.literal: At the great evaluation of capital officials, remonstrating officials impeached Qiyong for taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: At the great evaluation of capital officials, censors impeached Qiyong for accepting bribes.

sentences.zh: 吏部白其誣，詔為飭言者。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel reported that this was slander, and an edict rebuked the accusers.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel declared the charge false, and the emperor rebuked the accusers.

sentences.zh: 十九年，郭勛修前郤，因風霾勸帝罷免大臣，期雍遂去位。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Guo Xun settled old scores and, citing wind and dust storms, urged the emperor to dismiss grand ministers; Qiyong thereupon left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Guo Xun settled old scores and, citing ominous storms, urged the emperor to dismiss senior ministers; Qiyong then resigned.

sentences.zh: 家居十年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for ten years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for ten years and died.

sentences.zh: 唐龍，字虞佐，蘭溪人。

translations.literal: Tang Long, styled Yuzuo, was a native of Lanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Long, courtesy name Yuzuo, came from Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 受業於同縣章懋，登正德三年進士。

translations.literal: He studied under Zhang Mao of the same county and passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Zhang Mao of his county and passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 3.

sentences.zh: 除郯城知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Tancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Tancheng.

sentences.zh: 禦大盜劉六，數敗之，加俸二等。

translations.literal: Resisting the great bandit Liu Liu, he defeated him repeatedly and was given two grades' additional salary.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting the great bandit Liu Liu he won repeated victories and received a two-grade salary increase.

sentences.zh: 父喪，服除，征授御史，出按雲南。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father ended and the mourning garments were removed, he was summoned as Censor and sent to investigate Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period he was summoned as censor and sent to investigate Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 錢寧義父參將盧和坐罪當死，寧為奏辯，下鎮撫覆勘。

translations.literal: Qian Ning's adoptive father, Assistant Commander Lu He, was guilty of a capital crime; Ning pleaded on his behalf and the case was sent down to the Embroidered-Uniform Guard for re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Ning's adoptive father, assistant commander Lu He, faced a capital charge; Ning pleaded for him and the case was sent to the Embroidered-Uniform Guard for review.

sentences.zh: 會遣官錄囚，受寧屬欲出和，為龍所持，卒正其罪。

translations.literal: When officials were dispatched to review prisoners, one who had received Ning's request wished to release He, but Long held firm and in the end He was punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When prison reviewers arrived, an official beholden to Ning tried to release He, but Long held firm and He was punished.

sentences.zh: 土官鳳朝明坐罪死，革世職。

translations.literal: The native official Feng Chaoming was guilty of a capital crime and his hereditary office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Native official Feng Chaoming faced execution and lost his hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 寧令滇人為保舉，而矯旨許之。

translations.literal: Ning had Yunnan men petition in his defense and forged an edict permitting it.
translations.idiomatic: Ning had Yunnan natives petition for him and forged an edict of approval.

sentences.zh: 龍抗疏爭，寢其事。

translations.literal: Long memorialized in opposition and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Long memorialized in protest and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 再按江西，疏趣張忠、許泰班師。

translations.literal: Investigating Jiangxi a second time, he memorialized urging Zhang Zhong and Xu Tai to withdraw their armies.
translations.idiomatic: On a second tour of Jiangxi he urged Zhang Zhong and Xu Tai to withdraw their armies.

sentences.zh: 三司官從宸濠叛者猶居位，龍召數之曰：「脅從罔治，謂凡民耳。

translations.literal: Commissioners of the three offices who had followed Chenghao in rebellion still held their posts; Long summoned them and said, "Coerced followers are not punished—that applies to common people.
translations.idiomatic: Summoning commissioners who had followed Chenghao's rebellion, Long said, "Coerced followers go unpunished—that rule applies to commoners alone.

sentences.zh: 若輩讀書食祿，何顏乃爾。

translations.literal: You who have read books and received stipends—what face have you to be like this?
translations.idiomatic: You who read books and draw stipends—how can you show your faces?

sentences.zh: 」立收其印綬。

translations.literal: " He immediately seized their seals and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately seized their seals and credentials.

sentences.zh: 擢陜西提學副使，遷山西按察使，召為太仆卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Education of Shaanxi, transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Shanxi, and summoned as Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice commissioner of education in Shaanxi, surveillance commissioner of Shanxi, and was summoned as minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年改右僉都御史，總督漕運兼巡撫鳳陽諸府。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport, and concurrently Grand Coordinator of the Fengyang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 7 he was made right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of grain transport, and concurrently grand coordinator of the Fengyang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 奏罷淮西官馬種牛，罷壽州正陽關榷稅，通、泰二州虛田租及漕卒船料，民甚德之。

translations.literal: He memorialized to abolish official horse and cattle breeding west of the Huai, to end transit duties at Zhengyang Pass in Shouzhou, and to remit vacant land rents and boat fees for transport soldiers in Tong and Tai prefectures; the people greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished official horse and cattle breeding west of the Huai, ended transit duties at Zhengyang Pass, and remitted vacant land rents and transport fees in Tong and Tai prefectures; the people praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 召拜左副都御史，歷吏部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as left vice censor-in-chief and rose to left and right vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一年，陜西大饑。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Shaanxi suffered a great famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Shaanxi suffered a great famine.

sentences.zh: 吉囊擁眾臨邊，延綏告警。

translations.literal: Jibeng led a host to the border and Yan-Sui raised the alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Jibeng led a host to the frontier and Yan-Sui sounded the alarm.

sentences.zh: 詔進龍兵部尚書，總制三邊軍務兼理振濟，賫帑金三十萬以行。

translations.literal: An edict advanced Long to Minister of War with overall command of Three Frontiers military affairs and concurrent charge of relief, granting thirty thousand taels of treasury silver for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of war with overall command of the Three Frontiers and charge of famine relief, granted thirty thousand taels for the journey.

sentences.zh: 龍奏行救荒十四事。

translations.literal: Long memorialized fourteen measures for famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: Long submitted fourteen famine-relief measures.

sentences.zh: 時吉囊居套中，西抵賀蘭山，限以黃河不得渡，用十皮為渾脫，渡入山後。

translations.literal: At that time Jibeng dwelt in the Ordos; reaching west to Helan Mountain, blocked by the Yellow River from crossing, he used ten hides for a raft and crossed into the mountains beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Jibeng held the Ordos and, blocked by the Yellow River from crossing west to Helan Mountain, used ten hides to make rafts and crossed into the rear hills.

sentences.zh: 俺答亦自豐州入套為患。

translations.literal: Altan also entered the Ordos from Fengzhou and caused trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Altan also entered the Ordos from Fengzhou and raided.

sentences.zh: 龍用總兵官王效、梁震，數敗敵，屢被獎賚。

translations.literal: Long employed the supreme commanders Wang Xiao and Liang Zhen, who repeatedly defeated the enemy and were often rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Long employed supreme commanders Wang Xiao and Liang Zhen, who repeatedly defeated the enemy and won imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 大猾劉東山構陷建昌侯張延齡，興大獄。

translations.literal: The great schemer Liu Dongshan framed Marquis Zhang Yanling of Jianchang and stirred up a major case.
translations.idiomatic: The great schemer Liu Dongshan framed Marquis Zhang Yanling of Jianchang and stirred up a major case.

sentences.zh: 延齡，昭聖皇太后母弟，帝所惡也。

translations.literal: Yanling was the younger brother of the Empress Dowager Zhaosheng's mother, whom the emperor detested.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was the empress dowager's maternal younger brother, whom the emperor detested.

sentences.zh: 吏坐獄不窮竟去者數十人，龍獨執正東山罪。

translations.literal: Several dozen judicial officials left the case unfinished and withdrew; Long alone upheld Dongshan's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of judicial officials had left the case unfinished; Long alone upheld Dongshan's guilt.

sentences.zh: 「大禮」大獄及諸建言獲罪者，廷臣屢請寬，不能得。

translations.literal: In the Great Rites cases and those who had offended by remonstrance, court officials repeatedly asked leniency but could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Great Rites cases and other remonstrance prosecutions, the court repeatedly sought leniency in vain.

sentences.zh: 會九廟成，覃恩，龍錄上充軍應赦者百四十人，率得宥，所不原惟豐熙、楊慎、王元正、馬錄、呂經、馮恩、劉濟、邵經邦而已。

translations.literal: When the nine temples were completed and a general amnesty was proclaimed, Long listed one hundred forty men in military exile who qualified for pardon; nearly all were forgiven, and only Feng Xi, Yang Shen, Wang Yuanzheng, Ma Lu, Lü Jing, Feng En, Liu Ji, and Shao Jingbang were excluded.
translations.idiomatic: When the nine temples were completed Long listed one hundred forty exiles eligible for amnesty; nearly all were pardoned, leaving only Feng Xi, Yang Shen, Wang Yuanzheng, Ma Lu, Lü Jing, Feng En, Liu Ji, and Shao Jingbang.

sentences.zh: 考尚書六年滿，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When six years as minister were complete, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After six years as minister he was made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 以母老乞歸侍養。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he asked to return home to serve her.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his mother's age, he asked to return home to care for her.

sentences.zh: 久之，用薦起南京刑部尚書，就改吏部。

translations.literal: After a long time, on recommendation he was raised as Minister of Justice at Nanjing and then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was recommended as minister of justice at Nanjing and then transferred to personnel.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書戴金罷，召龍代之。

translations.literal: When Minister of War Dai Jin was dismissed, Long was summoned to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Dai Jin was dismissed, Long was summoned to replace him.

sentences.zh: 太廟成，加太子太保。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed, he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the ancestral temple was completed he was made grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋代熊浹為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Xiong Xian as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He soon replaced Xiong Xian as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 龍有才，居官著勞績。

translations.literal: Long had talent and in office achieved notable merit.
translations.idiomatic: Long was talented and achieved notable merit in office.

sentences.zh: 及為吏部，每事咨僚佐。

translations.literal: When he became Minister of Personnel he consulted his subordinates on every matter.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of personnel he consulted subordinates on every matter.

sentences.zh: 年老多疾，輒為所欺。

translations.literal: Old and often ill, he was repeatedly deceived by them.
translations.idiomatic: Old and often ill, he was repeatedly misled by them.

sentences.zh: 御史陳九德劾前選郎高簡罔上行私，並論龍衰暮，乃下簡詔獄。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Jiude impeached the former selection director Gao Jian for deceiving his superiors and pursuing private ends, and also criticized Long's senility; Gao Jian was then sent to prison by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Jiude impeached former selection director Gao Jian for deceiving superiors and criticized Long's senility; Gao was sent to prison.

sentences.zh: 龍引疾，未報。

translations.literal: Long cited illness and awaited a reply.
translations.idiomatic: Long cited illness and awaited a reply.

sentences.zh: 吏科楊上林、徐良輔復論簡。

translations.literal: The Personnel Section supervising secretaries Yang Shanglin and Xu Liangfu again argued the case against Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Yang Shanglin and Xu Liangfu again argued against Jian.

sentences.zh: 詔杖簡六十遣戍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jian beaten sixty strokes and sent to garrison exile.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Jian beaten sixty strokes and exiled to garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 上林、良輔以不早言罷職，龍黜為民。

translations.literal: Shanglin and Liangfu were dismissed for not speaking earlier; Long was demoted to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Shanglin and Liangfu were dismissed for not speaking sooner; Long was demoted to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 龍已有疾，輿出國門卒。

translations.literal: Long was already ill and died in his litter as it passed out the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: Already ill, he died in his litter as it passed the capital gate.

sentences.zh: 後數年，子修撰汝楫疏辯。

translations.literal: Several years later his son, Hanlin Compiler Zirui, memorialized in his father's defense.
translations.idiomatic: Years later his son, Hanlin compiler Zirui, memorialized in his defense.

sentences.zh: 詔復官，贈少保，謚文襄。

translations.literal: An edict restored his office and posthumously made him Junior Guardian with the posthumous title Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his rank and posthumously made him junior guardian with the title Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 龍故與嚴嵩善。

translations.literal: Long had formerly been on good terms with Yan Song.
translations.idiomatic: Long had once been friendly with Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 龍之罷，實夏言主之。

translations.literal: Long's dismissal was in fact chiefly engineered by Xia Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In fact Xia Yan had chiefly engineered Long's dismissal.

sentences.zh: 而汝楫素附嵩，得第一人及第。

translations.literal: Zirui had long attached himself to Song and took first place in the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zirui had long attached himself to Song and took first place in the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 官至左諭德。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 後坐嵩黨奪官。

translations.literal: Later, as a member of Song's faction, he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as a member of Song's faction, he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 王杲，字景初，汶上人。

translations.literal: Wang Gao, styled Jingchu, was a native of Wenshang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao, courtesy name Jingchu, came from Wenshang.

sentences.zh: 正德九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengde he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 9.

sentences.zh: 授臨汾知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Linfen.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，巡視陜西茶馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor and inspected the tea and horse trade in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor and inspected the tea and horse trade in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中官分守蘭、靖。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched palace eunuchs to garrison Lan and Jing in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched palace eunuchs to garrison Lan and Jing in rotation.

sentences.zh: 杲言窮邊饑歲，不宜設官累民，不報。

translations.literal: Gao said that on the impoverished frontier in years of famine it was inappropriate to set up offices that burdened the people; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: Gao argued that in famine years the impoverished frontier should not bear new offices burdening the people; he received no reply.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，帝將遣中官督織造於蘇、杭，杲疏諫，不納。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing the emperor was about to dispatch palace eunuchs to supervise weaving in Suzhou and Hangzhou; Gao memorialized in remonstrance, but it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 3 the emperor planned to send eunuchs to supervise weaving in Suzhou and Hangzhou; Gao remonstrated in vain.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢太仆少卿，改大理，再遷左副都御史，進戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, transferred to the Court of Judicial Review, then promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and advanced to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He later became vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, transferred to judicial review, rose to left vice censor-in-chief, and became right vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 河南大饑，命杲往振。

translations.literal: Henan suffered a great famine and Gao was ordered to go provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan suffered a great famine Gao was ordered to provide relief.

sentences.zh: 杲請急發帑金，詔賫臨清倉銀五萬兩以行。

translations.literal: Gao asked urgently to release treasury silver; an edict granted fifty thousand taels from the Linqing granary for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Gao urgently requested treasury silver; the court granted fifty thousand taels from the Linqing granary.

sentences.zh: 既至，復請發十五萬兩。

translations.literal: When he arrived he again asked to release one hundred fifty thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he requested another one hundred fifty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 全活不可勝計。

translations.literal: Those saved cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Countless lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 事竣，賜銀幣。

translations.literal: When the task was finished he was granted silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: When the relief work ended he was rewarded with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 尋以右都御史總督漕運。

translations.literal: Soon he served as Right Censor-in-Chief with overall charge of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became right censor-in-chief with overall charge of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 故事，繕運艘，軍三民七。

translations.literal: By precedent, repairing transport vessels was three parts military and seven parts civilian.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent transport vessels were repaired at three parts military cost and seven parts civilian.

sentences.zh: 總兵官顧寰以軍民困敝，請發兩淮余鹽銀七十萬，戶部尚書李如圭不可。

translations.literal: Supreme Commander Gu Huai, because military and civilian labor were exhausted, asked to issue seven hundred thousand taels from surplus salt revenue in the two Huai circuits; Minister of Revenue Li Rugui refused.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Commander Gu Huai, citing exhausted military and civilian labor, asked for seven hundred thousand taels from Huai salt surplus; Minister Li Rugui refused.

sentences.zh: 杲請改折兩年漕運十之三，以所省轉輸費治運艘，勿重困軍民，報可。

translations.literal: Gao asked to commute three-tenths of the grain transport for two years and use the savings in transport costs to repair vessels, so as not to burden military and civilian labor further; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Gao proposed commuting three-tenths of grain transport for two years and using the savings to repair vessels without further burdening troops and civilians; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 逾年，入為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he entered office as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 後父安平侯方銳乞張家莊馬房地。

translations.literal: Later his father-in-law, Marquis Fang Rui of Anping, asked for horse-pasture land at Zhangjiazhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Later his father-in-law, Marquis Fang Rui of Anping, petitioned for horse-pasture land at Zhangjiazhuang.

sentences.zh: 杲言此地二千余頃，正供所出，不可許，宜以大慈恩寺入官地二十頃予之。

translations.literal: Gao said this land of more than two thousand qing was revenue for regular tribute and could not be granted; it would be better to give twenty qing of land from the Daci'en Temple that had entered official registers.
translations.idiomatic: Gao said the two thousand-odd qing supplied regular tribute revenue and could not be granted; he proposed granting twenty qing of temple land from Daci'en instead.

sentences.zh: 帝從其議。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 時國儲告匱，諸邊請增餉無虛月，四方多水旱，給事中李文進請議廣儲蓄。

translations.literal: At that time state reserves were depleted, the frontiers repeatedly asked for added pay every month, and flood and drought were widespread; Supervising Secretary Li Wenjin asked that measures to expand reserves be debated.
translations.idiomatic: State reserves were depleted, the frontiers sought added pay monthly, and flood and drought were widespread; Supervising Secretary Li Wenjin asked the court to debate expanding reserves.

sentences.zh: 杲列九事以獻，已又上制財用十事，帝鹹納之。

translations.literal: Gao listed nine items and presented them; afterward he also submitted ten measures for controlling expenditures, and the emperor accepted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gao submitted nine proposals, then ten measures for controlling expenditures; the emperor accepted them all.

sentences.zh: 舊制，歲漕四百萬石。

translations.literal: By the old system, annual grain transport was four million piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system annual grain transport totaled four million piculs.

sentences.zh: 杲以粟有余而用不足，遇災傷率改折以便民。

translations.literal: Gao, because grain was plentiful but expenditures insufficient, whenever disaster struck would routinely commute grain payments to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: Though grain stores were ample, expenditures ran short; Gao routinely allowed grain-tax commutation after disasters to ease the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝見改折者過半，大驚，以詰戶部，杲等引罪。

translations.literal: One day the emperor saw that more than half had been commuted and was greatly alarmed; he questioned the Ministry of Revenue, and Gao and the others confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor found that more than half the grain transport had been commuted and was alarmed; he questioned the Ministry of Revenue, and Gao and his colleagues took the blame.

sentences.zh: 敕自今務遵祖制，毋輕變。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that from now on the ancestral system must be strictly followed and not lightly changed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded strict adherence to ancestral precedent and forbade casual changes.

sentences.zh: 杲掌邦計，事無不辦，帝深倚之。

translations.literal: Gao managed state finances and nothing went undone; the emperor relied on him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Gao ran state finances with nothing left undone, and the emperor relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 後有詔買龍涎香，久不進，帝以此不悅。

translations.literal: Later there was an edict to purchase ambergris; for a long time none was delivered, and the emperor was displeased on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court ordered ambergris purchased, but delivery was long delayed and the emperor grew displeased.

sentences.zh: 給事中馬錫劾杲及巡倉御史艾樸受賄，給事中厲汝進言倉場尚書王暐亦然，並下獄。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Ma Xi impeached Gao and the grain-depot inspector Ai Pu for taking bribes; Supervising Secretary Li Rujin said Granary Director Wang Wei was likewise, and all were sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Ma Xi impeached Gao and depot inspector Ai Pu for bribery; Li Rujin said Granary Director Wang Wei was guilty as well, and all were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 杲、樸遣戍，暐斥為民。

translations.literal: Gao and Pu were sent to garrison exile; Wei was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Gao and Pu were banished to frontier garrison service; Wei was stripped of office and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 杲竟卒於雷州戍所。

translations.literal: Gao in the end died at the garrison post in Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao ultimately died at his place of exile in Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，給事中辛自修等訟杲冤。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, Supervising Secretary Xin Zixiu and others petitioned on Gao's wrongful conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign supervising secretaries led by Xin Zixiu petitioned to redress Gao's conviction.

sentences.zh: 詔復官，賜祭葬，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: An edict restored his office, granted sacrificial burial, and posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The throne restored his rank, granted state funeral rites, and posthumously made him grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 王暐，句容人。

translations.literal: Wang Wei was a native of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei came from Jurong.

sentences.zh: 由進士除吉安推官。

translations.literal: Through the jinshi degree he was appointed investigating prefect of Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: As a jinshi he was appointed investigating prefect of Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 從王守仁平宸濠，遷大理寺副。

translations.literal: He followed Wang Yangming in pacifying Chen Hao and was transferred to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Yangming in suppressing Chen Hao's rebellion and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 爭「大禮」，下獄廷杖。

translations.literal: He disputed the "Great Rites" and was imprisoned and beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Great Rites protest, was imprisoned, and suffered court beating.

sentences.zh: 累遷右副都御史，巡撫江西。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 歷兩京戶部侍郎，出督漕運，進尚書。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice minister of revenue in both capitals, went out to supervise grain transport, and was advanced to minister.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of revenue in both capitals, supervised grain transport, and was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 歷官著清操。

translations.literal: Throughout his offices he was noted for pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his career he maintained an upright reputation.

sentences.zh: 周用，字行之，吳江人。

translations.literal: Zhou Yong, styled Xingzhi, was a native of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yong, courtesy name Xingzhi, came from Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Hongzhi 15.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Bearer of Imperial Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed bearer of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 正德初，擢南京兵科給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengde he was made supervising secretary in the Nanjing Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 父憂服闋，留補禮科。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father ended and he returned to service, he remained to fill a post in the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's mourning ended he stayed on as supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 已，乞南。

translations.literal: Later he asked to serve in the south.
translations.idiomatic: He later asked to be posted to the south.

sentences.zh: 改南京兵科。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Bureau of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Nanjing Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 諫迎佛烏斯藏及以中旨遷黜尚書、都給事中等官，且請治鎮守江西中官黎安罪。

translations.literal: He remonstrated against welcoming a Buddhist from U-Tsang and against using imperial rescripts to transfer and dismiss ministers and the chief supervising secretary, and also asked that the crime of Li An, the eunuch supervising Jiangxi, be punished.
translations.idiomatic: He protested welcoming a Buddhist from U-Tsang and imperial rescripts demoting ministers and the chief supervising secretary, and demanded punishment for the eunuch Li An, military commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 出為廣東參議，預平番禺盜，有功。

translations.literal: He went out as administration vice commissioner of Guangdong and took part beforehand in pacifying bandits in Panyu, with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Guangdong as administration vice commissioner, he helped pacify bandits in Panyu with distinction.

sentences.zh: 歷浙江、山東副使。

translations.literal: He served successively as administration vice commissioner of Zhejiang and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administration vice commissioner in Zhejiang and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 擢福建按察使，改河南右布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Fujian and transferred to right administration commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made surveillance commissioner of Fujian, then right administration commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 代監司鞫南陽滯獄，獄為之空。

translations.literal: Acting for the supervising offices he tried backlog cases in Nanyang, and the prisons were emptied on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Acting for the supervising offices he cleared Nanyang's backlog of cases until the prisons stood empty.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年擢右副都御史，巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 8 he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of southern Jiangxi and Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 召協理院事。

translations.literal: He was summoned to assist in managing the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to assist in Censorate affairs.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as left and right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left and right vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 以起廢不當，尚書汪鋐委罪僚屬，乃調用南京刑部。

translations.literal: Because the restoration of dismissed officials was improper, Minister Wang Qiao shifted blame onto his subordinates, and Yong was transferred to the Ministry of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When improper restorations of dismissed officials drew criticism, Minister Wang Qiao blamed his staff and Yong was moved to the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 就遷右都御史，工、刑二部尚書。

translations.literal: He was then made Right Censor-in-Chief and minister of the Ministries of Works and of Justice in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right censor-in-chief and then minister of works and of justice.

sentences.zh: 九廟災，自陳致仕。

translations.literal: When the Nine Temples burned he asked on his own initiative to retire.
translations.idiomatic: After fire destroyed the Nine Temples he offered his resignation.

sentences.zh: 用端亮有節概。

translations.literal: Yong was upright and had principled bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was upright and principled in character.

sentences.zh: 既罷，中外皆惜之，頻有推薦。

translations.literal: After his dismissal, inside and outside the court all regretted it, and recommendations for him came repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: After he left office court and country alike regretted his loss, and he was repeatedly recommended for recall.

sentences.zh: 久之，以工部尚書起督河道，數月，改漕運。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned as minister of works to supervise the waterways; several months later he was changed to grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was recalled as minister of works to supervise waterways, then after a few months shifted to grain transport.

sentences.zh: 未上，召拜左都御史。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was summoned and appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up that post he was summoned as left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二品九年滿，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When nine years at the second rank were complete, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years at second rank he was made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十五年代唐龍為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he replaced Tang Long as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 he succeeded Tang Long as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 明年卒官。

translations.literal: The next year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office the following year.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚恭肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent with the title Gongsu.

sentences.zh: 曾孫宗建，自有傳。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Zongjian has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Zongjian has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 用掌憲時，慎自持而已，無所獻替。

translations.literal: When Yong held the censorate he was cautious in self-restraint only and offered no advice or criticism.
translations.idiomatic: As censor-in-chief Yong held himself carefully in check but offered little counsel.

sentences.zh: 其後宋景、屠僑繼之，大略皆廉潔，與用相似。

translations.literal: Afterward Song Jing and Tu Qiao succeeded him; broadly they were all incorrupt, similar to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing and Tu Qiao followed him; all were broadly incorrupt like Yong.

sentences.zh: 景未久卒，而僑居職八年。

translations.literal: Jing died not long after, while Qiao held office eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Jing died soon after taking office; Qiao served eight years.

sentences.zh: 屬嚴嵩柄政，風紀不振。

translations.literal: Yan Song held power, and discipline was not upheld.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yan Song's dominance court discipline collapsed.

sentences.zh: 議丁汝夔獄，受杖不能去。

translations.literal: When the case of Ding Ruai was debated, he was beaten and could not leave his post.
translations.idiomatic: Debating the case of Ding Ruai, he was beaten at court and could not rise to leave.

sentences.zh: 宋景，字以賢，奉新人。

translations.literal: Song Jing, styled Yixian, was a native of Fengxin.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing, courtesy name Yixian, came from Fengxin.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年進士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Hongzhi 18.

sentences.zh: 知睢州。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 正德五年入為河南道御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengde he entered office as censor of the Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 5 he became censor of the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 故事，知州無改御史者，劉瑾創之也。

translations.literal: By precedent, prefects were not transferred to censor; Liu Jin created this practice.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent prefects were not made censors; Liu Jin introduced the practice.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，景引疾去。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Jing pleaded illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's execution Jing cited illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年以薦補浙江僉事，進山西副使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing, on recommendation he was restored as administration intendant of Zhejiang and promoted to administration vice commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 3 he was recommended back as Zhejiang administration intendant and promoted to Shanxi administration vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 民饑為盜，殺守稟指揮。

translations.literal: The people, starving, became bandits and killed the garrison commander and a brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: Starving people turned to banditry and killed the garrison commander and a brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 景樹幟，令被脅者赴之。

translations.literal: Jing raised banners and ordered those who had been coerced to come to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing raised banners and summoned those who had been forced to join the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊鹹歸命，乃擒斬其魁。

translations.literal: The bandits all submitted, and then he seized and executed their leaders.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits all surrendered; he then captured and executed the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 四遷山西左布政使，累官南京吏、工二部尚書。

translations.literal: After four promotions he became Left Administration Commissioner of Shanxi and rose in office to minister of personnel and of works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted four times he became left administration commissioner of Shanxi and eventually minister of personnel and of works at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 改兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of War to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Ministry of War to assist in military planning.

sentences.zh: 入為左都御史。

translations.literal: He entered office as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保、吏部尚書，謚莊靖。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous title Zhuangjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made junior guardian and minister of personnel with the title Zhuangjing.

sentences.zh: 屠僑，字安卿，吏部尚書滽再從子也。

translations.literal: Tu Qiao, styled Anqing, was the grand-nephew of Minister of Personnel Tu Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Qiao, courtesy name Anqing, was a grand-nephew of Minister of Personnel Tu Ze.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 6.

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 巡視居庸諸關。

translations.literal: He inspected the passes at Juyong and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the Juyong and other frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 武宗遣中官李嵩等捕虎豹，僑力言不可。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong sent the eunuch Li Song and others to capture tigers and leopards; Qiao strongly argued that this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong sent eunuch Li Song to capture tigers and leopards, Qiao protested firmly.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，歷左都御史。

translations.literal: In the Shizong reign he served successively as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jiajing emperor he rose to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈少保，謚簡肅。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian, with the posthumous title Jiansu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made junior guardian with the title Jiansu.

sentences.zh: 聞淵，字靜中，鄞人。

translations.literal: Wen Yuan, styled Jingzhong, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yuan, courtesy name Jingzhong, came from Yin county.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年進士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Hongzhi 18.

sentences.zh: 初授禮部主事，已，改刑部。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Rites; later he was transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was first a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, then transferred to justice.

sentences.zh: 楊一清為吏部，調淵稽勛員外郎。

translations.literal: When Yang Yiqing was minister of personnel, Yuan was transferred to registrar in the Bureau of Imperial Lineages.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yiqing headed personnel, Yuan was made registrar in the Bureau of Imperial Lineages.

sentences.zh: 歷考功郎中，改掌文選，遷南京右通政。

translations.literal: He served successively as director in the Bureau of Personnel Evaluation, was changed to manage selection, and was promoted to Right Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the evaluation bureau, took charge of appointments, and became right vice commissioner of imperial entertainments at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，擢應天府尹，改尹順天。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was promoted to prefect of Yingtian and changed to prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing he was made prefect of Yingtian, then of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京兵部右侍郎，攝部事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing and acted as head of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right vice minister of war at Nanjing and acted as minister.

sentences.zh: 薦馬永等十余人。

translations.literal: He recommended more than ten men including Ma Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended more than ten men, including Ma Yong.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部右侍郎，遷左。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Justice and promoted to the left.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as right vice minister of justice and promoted to the left.

sentences.zh: 進南京刑部尚書，就移吏部。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Justice at Nanjing and then moved to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of justice at Nanjing, then moved to personnel.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 周用卒，代為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zhou Yong died, Yuan replaced him as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yong died, Yuan succeeded him as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 侍郎徐階得帝眷，前尚書率推讓之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Xu Jie had won the emperor's favor, and former ministers had all yielded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Xu Jie enjoyed imperial favor, and earlier ministers had deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 淵自以前輩，事取獨斷。

translations.literal: Yuan, considering himself the senior, took sole decision in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, as the senior man, decided matters on his own.

sentences.zh: 大學士夏言柄政，淵老臣，不能委曲徇。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xia Yan held power; Yuan was an old official and could not bend and follow along.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xia Yan dominated the court; Yuan, an elder statesman, would not bend to him.

sentences.zh: 及後議言獄，淵謂言事只任意，跡涉要君，請帝自裁決。

translations.literal: Later, when Xia Yan's case was debated, Yuan said Yan's conduct was merely arbitrary and the traces suggested coercing the sovereign; he asked the emperor to decide for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Later, debating Xia Yan's case, Yuan said Xia Yan had acted arbitrarily in ways that looked like coercing the throne and asked the emperor to judge for himself.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，切責淵。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sharply rebuked Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and sharply rebuked Yuan.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩既殺言，勢益橫，部權無不侵，數以小故奪淵俸。

translations.literal: After Yan Song had killed Yan, his power grew still more overbearing; he encroached on every ministry prerogative and several times on small pretexts docked Yuan's salary.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Song destroyed Xia Yan his power grew unchecked; he seized every ministry prerogative and repeatedly cut Yuan's salary on petty grounds.

sentences.zh: 淵年七十矣，遂乞骸骨歸。

translations.literal: Yuan was seventy years old and thereupon begged to return home on old bones.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy Yuan begged leave to retire.

sentences.zh: 家居十四年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home fourteen years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement fourteen years and died.

sentences.zh: 先累加太子太保，卒贈少保，謚莊簡。

translations.literal: Earlier he had repeatedly been given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; on death he was posthumously made Junior Guardian, with the posthumous title Zhuangjian.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier been made grand guardian of the heir apparent; on death he was posthumously made junior guardian with the title Zhuangjian.

sentences.zh: 淵居官始終一節。

translations.literal: Yuan in office from beginning to end held to one principle.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan maintained a single standard of conduct throughout his career.

sentences.zh: 晚扼權相，功名頗損。

translations.literal: In his later years he checked a powerful minister, and his reputation suffered considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he opposed a powerful minister and his reputation suffered.

sentences.zh: 在南刑部時，張璁先為曹屬，嘗題詩於壁，屬淵勒石後堂。

translations.literal: When he was at the Ministry of Justice in the south, Zhang Cong had earlier been a subordinate official and once inscribed a poem on the wall, asking Yuan to carve it in stone in the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: While minister of justice at Nanjing, Zhang Cong—then a junior official—had written a poem on a wall and asked Yuan to carve it in the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「此尚書堂也，吾敢以相君故，為郎官勒石耶？」

translations.literal: Yuan said: "This is the hall of a minister—how dare I, because of a chief minister, carve stone for a bureau secretary?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan replied: "This is a minister's hall. How could I carve stone for a bureau secretary just because he became chief minister?"

sentences.zh: 劉讱，鄢陵人。

translations.literal: Liu Ren was a native of Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ren came from Yanling.

sentences.zh: 父璟，刑部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing had been minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 讱登正德十二年進士，為寧國推官，攝蕪湖縣事。

translations.literal: Ren passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Zhengde, was appointed investigating prefect of Ningguo, and acted in the affairs of Wuhu county.
translations.idiomatic: Ren passed the jinshi in Zhengde 12, became investigating prefect of Ningguo, and handled affairs in Wuhu county.

sentences.zh: 武宗南巡，中貴索賄不得，系讱詔獄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong toured the south, a palace eunuch, having failed to obtain a bribe, had Ren imprisoned by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuzong's southern tour a palace eunuch who failed to extort a bribe had Ren thrown into prison by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，復官。

translations.literal: When Shizong came to the throne, Ren's office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing emperor ascended, Ren was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 尋擢御史，遷南京通政參議。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to censor and transferred to vice commissioner in the Nanjing Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made censor, then moved to vice commissioner of transmission at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 歷南京刑部尚書，召改北。

translations.literal: He served successively as Minister of Justice at Nanjing and was summoned to take up the post in the north.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of justice at Nanjing and was then recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，帝幸承天，河南巡撫胡纘宗嘗以事笞陽武知縣王聯。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor visited Chengtian, Henan grand coordinator Hu Zongzong had once flogged Wang Lian, magistrate of Yangwu, over some matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first toured Chengtian, Henan grand coordinator Hu Zongzong had beaten Yangwu magistrate Wang Lian over a dispute.

sentences.zh: 聯尋為巡按御史陶欽夔劾罷。

translations.literal: Lian was soon impeached and dismissed by touring censor Tao Qinkui.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was soon impeached and removed by touring censor Tao Qinkui.

sentences.zh: 聯素兇狡，嘗歐其父良，論死。

translations.literal: Lian had always been fierce and cunning; he had once beaten his father Liang and was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was vicious by nature; he had beaten his father Liang and been sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 久之，以良請出獄。

translations.literal: After a long time, at Liang's plea he was released from prison.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually his father Liang secured his release from prison.

sentences.zh: 復坐殺人，求解不得。

translations.literal: He was again convicted of murder and could not obtain a pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted of murder again and could not win a reprieve.

sentences.zh: 知帝喜告訐，乃摭纘宗迎駕詩「穆王八駿」語為謗詛。

translations.literal: Knowing the emperor delighted in accusations, he seized on Zongzong's poem welcoming the imperial progress, the phrase about King Mu's eight steeds, as slander.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor welcomed informers, he twisted Zongzong's welcoming poem and its line on King Mu's eight steeds into treasonous slander.

sentences.zh: 言纘宗命己刊布，不從，屬欽夔論黜，羅織成大辟。

translations.literal: He said Zongzong had ordered him to publish it and he had refused; he charged that Qinkui had engineered his dismissal and wove a capital case.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed Zongzong ordered publication and he refused; he blamed Qinkui for his dismissal and fabricated a capital charge.

sentences.zh: 候長至日，令其子詐為常朝官，闌入闕門訟冤。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice he had his son pose as a regular court official and force his way through the palace gate to plead injustice.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice he sent his son, disguised as a routine court officer, through the palace gates to cry injustice.

sentences.zh: 凡所不悅，若副都御史劉隅，給事中鮑道明，御史胡植、馮章、張洽，參議朱鴻漸，知府項喬、賈應春等百十人，悉構入之。

translations.literal: Everyone he disliked—such as vice censor-in-chief Liu Yu, supervising secretary Bao Daoming, censors Hu Zhi, Feng Zhang, and Zhang Qia, administration commissioner Zhu Hongjian, and prefects Xiang Qiao and Jia Yingchun, more than a hundred in all—he worked into the case.
translations.idiomatic: He dragged into the case every enemy—vice censor Liu Yu, supervising secretary Bao Daoming, censors Hu Zhi, Feng Zhang, and Zhang Qia, commissioner Zhu Hongjian, prefects Xiang Qiao and Jia Yingchun, and scores more.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，立遣官捕纘宗等下獄，命讱會法司嚴訊。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and immediately sent officers to arrest Zongzong and the others and imprison them, ordering Ren to join the judiciary in a strict inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, had Zongzong and others seized at once, and ordered Ren to conduct a rigorous joint trial with the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 讱等盡得其誣罔，仍坐聯死，當其子詐冒朝官律斬，而為纘宗等乞宥。

translations.literal: Ren and the others fully exposed the fabrications, still imposed death on Lian, ruled that the son deserved decapitation under the statute for falsely posing as a court officer, yet pleaded mercy for Zongzong and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Ren's inquiry proved the charges false; Lian still faced death and his son the penalty for gate-crashing as a fake court officer, but Ren pleaded leniency for Zongzong and the others.

sentences.zh: 帝既從法司奏坐聯父子辟，然心嗛纘宗，頗多詰讓，下禮部都察院參議。
