translations.literal: The emperor had already accepted the judiciary's memorial sentencing Lian and his son to death, yet he still resented Zongzong and rebuked him sharply, sending the case to the Ministry of Rites and the Censorate for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Though he approved the death sentence on the Lians, the emperor still bore a grudge against Zongzong, rebuked him harshly, and referred the matter to the Ministry of Rites and Censorate.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩為之解，乃革纘宗職，杖四十。

translations.literal: Yan Song interceded for him, and Zongzong was merely stripped of office and beaten forty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song smoothed things over; Zongzong lost his post and took forty blows.

sentences.zh: 讱亦除名，法司正貳停半歲俸，郎官承問者下詔獄。

translations.literal: Ren was also dismissed; the chief and deputy heads of the judiciary lost half a year's salary, and the reviewing secretaries were sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Ren was removed from office; senior judges forfeited half a year's pay and the clerks who handled the case went to prison.

sentences.zh: 嵩以對制平獄有功，令兼支大學士俸，嵩辭乃允。

translations.literal: Because Song had helped settle the case to the emperor's satisfaction, he was allowed to draw a grand secretary's salary in addition; Song declined and the offer was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Song was offered an extra grand-secretary stipend for managing the trial to the emperor's liking; he refused and the grant was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時法官率骫法徇上意。

translations.literal: At that time judges generally bent the law to follow the sovereign's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Judges then routinely twisted the law to suit the throne.

sentences.zh: 稍執正，譴責隨至。

translations.literal: If they held even slightly to principle, reprimand followed at once.
translations.idiomatic: The slightest independence brought immediate punishment.

sentences.zh: 讱於是獄能持法，身雖黜，而天下稱之。

translations.literal: Ren in this case was able to uphold the law; though he himself was dismissed, the realm praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Ren held to the law in that trial; though dismissed himself, he won wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 胡纘宗，陜西秦安人。

translations.literal: Hu Zongzong was a native of Qin'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongzong came from Qin'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Zhengde 3.

sentences.zh: 由檢討出為嘉定判官。

translations.literal: From the post of reviser he went out as assistant magistrate of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Hanlin as Jiading assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 歷山東巡撫，改河南。

translations.literal: He served as grand coordinator of Shandong and was transferred to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was grand coordinator of Shandong, then of Henan.

sentences.zh: 孫應奎，字文宿，洛陽人。

translations.literal: Sun Yingkui, styled Wensu, was a native of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yingkui, courtesy name Wensu, came from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Zhengde 16.

sentences.zh: 授章丘知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Zhangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Zhangqiu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年入為兵科給事中，上疏言：「輔臣之任，必忠厚鯁亮、純白堅定者乃足當之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing he entered office as supervising secretary in the Bureau of War and memorialized: "The duty of a chief minister requires someone loyal, forthright, pure, and firm."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 4 he became a war-bureau supervising secretary and wrote: "A chief minister must be loyal, upright, pure, and steadfast."

sentences.zh: 今大學士楊一清雖練達國體，而雅性尚通，難以獨任。

translations.literal: Today Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing, though experienced in state affairs, is by nature fond of accommodation and hard to rely on alone.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing knows statecraft but is too easygoing to bear the burden alone.

sentences.zh: 張璁學博性偏，傷於自恃，猶飭厲功名，當抑其過而用之。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong is learned but partial and harmed by self-confidence; he still pursues reputation—his faults should be checked while he is used.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong is learned yet biased and self-willed; curb his excesses but keep him in service.

sentences.zh: 至於桂萼以梟雄桀驁之資，作威福，納財賄，阻抑氣節，私比黨與，勢侵六官，氣制言路，天下莫不怨憤。

translations.literal: As for Gui E, with the talent of a fierce, overbearing man he wields power, takes bribes, crushes integrity, forms private factions, encroaches on the six ministries, and intimidates the remonstrance offices—the realm resents him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E is ruthless and domineering: he abuses power, takes bribes, crushes honest men, builds factions, bullies the ministries, and silences the censors—everyone hates him.

sentences.zh: 乞鑒別三臣賢否，以定用舍。

translations.literal: I beg that Your Majesty distinguish whether these three ministers are worthy, to decide whom to keep or dismiss."
translations.idiomatic: Please judge these three ministers and decide whom to keep or remove."

sentences.zh: 」其意特右璁。

translations.literal: His intent was especially to favor Cong.
translations.idiomatic: He clearly meant to side with Zhang Cong.

sentences.zh: 而帝因其奏，慰留一清，戒諭璁、萼。

translations.literal: Yet because of his memorial the emperor reassured Yiqing to remain and admonished Cong and E.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor used the memorial to keep Yang Yiqing and warn Zhang Cong and Gui E.

sentences.zh: 既而同官王準、陸粲劾璁、萼罷相，準、粲亦下吏遠謫，以應奎首抗章不罪。

translations.literal: Soon colleagues Wang Zhun and Lu Can impeached Cong and E and brought down the chief ministers; Zhun and Can were also imprisoned and exiled far away, but because Yingkui had led the protest he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhun and Lu Can toppled Cong and E they too were jailed and banished; Yingkui, having spoken first, went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 未幾，劾吏部尚書方獻夫，帝頗納其言。

translations.literal: Before long he impeached Minister of Personnel Fang Xianfu, and the emperor largely accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: He soon attacked Minister of Personnel Fang Xianfu, and the emperor largely agreed.

sentences.zh: 獻夫援汪鋐為助，遂詘應奎議。

translations.literal: Xianfu enlisted Wang Qian as support and thus refuted Yingkui's charges.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfu rallied Wang Qian and beat back Yingkui's case.

sentences.zh: 再遷戶科左給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to left supervising secretary in the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left supervising secretary in the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 行人孽侃建言忤旨，下廷訊，詞連張璁。

translations.literal: The courier Nie Kan spoke in remonstrance against the imperial will and was tried at court; his words implicated Zhang Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Courier Nie Kan remonstrated against the throne and faced court trial; his testimony touched Zhang Cong.

sentences.zh: 應奎與同官曹汴揖璁避，且上疏言狀。

translations.literal: Yingkui and colleague Cao Bian bowed to Cong and stepped aside, and also memorialized stating the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui and Cao Bian bowed to Cong and withdrew, then memorialized on the affair.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下之詔獄，尋釋還職。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent him to the imperial prison, but soon released him and restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor jailed him, then soon freed him and restored his post.

sentences.zh: 十一年大計天下庶官，王準謫富民典史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, at the great review of officials throughout the realm, Wang Zhun was demoted to recorder of Fumin.
translations.idiomatic: At the eleventh-year general review Wang Zhun was demoted to Fumin recorder.

sentences.zh: 應奎言汪鋐為璁、萼修郤，誣以不謹而黜之。

translations.literal: Yingkui said Wang Qian, to settle scores for Cong and E, had falsely charged Zhun with impropriety to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui charged that Wang Qian, doing Cong and E's dirty work, had falsely dismissed Zhun for "impropriety."

sentences.zh: 乞復準官，責鋐，為黨比戒。

translations.literal: He asked that Zhun's office be restored, Qian be punished, and factional collusion be warned against.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to restore Zhun, punish Qian, and warn against cliques.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王瓊亦言準當黜，乃謫應奎高平縣丞。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Qiong also said Zhun should be dismissed, and Yingkui was demoted to assistant magistrate of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel minister Wang Qiong backed the demotion, and Yingkui was sent down to Gaoping assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 屢遷湖廣副使，督采大木，坐累復逮系。

translations.literal: After several promotions he became vice commissioner of Huguang and supervised timber procurement; implicated in that duty he was again arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Huguang vice commissioner, he oversaw timber levies, was implicated, and jailed again.

sentences.zh: 尋釋還。

translations.literal: Before long he was released.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon released.

sentences.zh: 歷右副都御史，巡撫順天。

translations.literal: He rose to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He became right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 召理院事，遷戶部侍郎，進尚書。

translations.literal: Summoned to manage the Censorate, he was moved to vice minister of revenue and then minister.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to head the Censorate, he became vice then minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 俺答犯京師後，羽書旁午征兵餉。

translations.literal: After Altan raided the capital region, urgent dispatches flew in every direction to levy troops and funds.
translations.idiomatic: After Altan Khan struck near the capital, urgent orders multiplied for troops and money.

sentences.zh: 應奎乃建議加派。

translations.literal: Yingkui then proposed an additional levy.
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui proposed a supplemental tax.

sentences.zh: 自北方諸府暨廣西、貴州外，其他量地貧富，驟增銀一百十五萬有奇，而蘇州一府乃八萬五千。

translations.literal: Apart from the northern prefectures and Guangxi and Guizhou, other regions were taxed by land and wealth, suddenly adding more than 1,150,000 taels of silver—and Suzhou prefecture alone owed eighty-five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the north, Guangxi, and Guizhou, levies by local wealth added over 1.15 million taels—Suzhou alone paid eighty-five thousand.

sentences.zh: 御史郭仁，吳人也，詣應奎請減，不從。

translations.literal: Censor Guo Ren, a man of Wu, went to Yingkui to ask for a reduction and was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Guo Ren of Wu asked for relief; Yingkui refused.

sentences.zh: 仁遂劾奏，應奎疏辨。

translations.literal: Ren then impeached him, and Yingkui memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Ren impeached him; Yingkui replied in defense.

sentences.zh: 帝以仁不當私屬，調之外。

translations.literal: The emperor held that Ren should not have made a private request and transferred him elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled Ren had lobbied improperly and posted him away.

sentences.zh: 既而國用猶不足，應奎言：「今歲入二百萬，而諸邊費六百余萬，一切取財法行之已盡。

translations.literal: Yet state revenue was still insufficient; Yingkui said: "This year's intake is two million, while frontier costs exceed six million—all revenue measures are exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: Revenue still fell short; Yingkui reported intake of two million against frontier costs above six million and said every fiscal device was spent.

sentences.zh: 請令諸曹所隸官吏、儒士、廚役、校卒，悉去其冗者。

translations.literal: He asked that redundant clerks, scholars, cooks, and runners in every ministry be removed.
translations.idiomatic: He urged cutting redundant staff in every ministry and office.

sentences.zh: 而臣部出入贏縮之數，亦綜其大綱，列籍進禦，使百司庶府鹹知為國惜財。

translations.literal: He also asked that the surplus and deficit of his ministry's accounts be summarized in a register presented to the throne, so that all offices would know to cherish state funds.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for a summary ledger of ministry income and outgo so all agencies would husband public money.

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: The reply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 三十一年正月命應奎條上京邊備用芻糧之數。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirty-first year the emperor ordered Yingkui to itemize fodder and grain reserves for the capital and frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 31 the emperor ordered him to list capital and frontier grain stores.

sentences.zh: 應奎言：「自臣入都至今，計正稅、加賦、余鹽五百余萬外，他所搜括又四百余萬。

translations.literal: Yingkui said: "From my arrival in the capital until now, besides regular tax, supplemental levy, and surplus salt totaling more than five million, other exactions have added another four million."
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui reported that since he took office regular tax, surcharges, and salt had brought in over five million, with another four million squeezed elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 而所出自諸邊年例二百八十萬外，新增二百四十五萬有奇，修邊振濟諸役又八百余萬。

translations.literal: Yet apart from the annual frontier quota of 2,800,000, new charges added another 2,450,000-odd, and border repair and relief works another eight million-odd."
translations.idiomatic: Yet beyond the 2.8 million annual frontier quota, new charges topped 2.45 million and repair and relief another eight million."

sentences.zh: 」帝以耗費多，疑有侵冒，分遣科道官往諸邊核實。

translations.literal: The emperor, thinking expenditure excessive, suspected embezzlement and sent censors and supervising secretaries to the frontiers to verify accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting waste and graft, the emperor sent censors to audit the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 給事中徐公遴劾應奎粗疏自用，遂改南京工部尚書，以方鈍代。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Xu Gonglin impeached Yingkui as crude and self-willed; he was transferred to minister of works at Nanjing, with Fang Dun replacing him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gonglin attacked Yingkui as rash; he was moved to Nanjing minister of works and Fang Dun took his place.

sentences.zh: 諸邊餉銀益增。

translations.literal: Frontier funds increased still more.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier appropriations kept rising.

sentences.zh: 鈍計無所出，請令諸臣條上理財策。

translations.literal: Dun, finding no way to meet costs, asked all ministers to submit plans for managing finances.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to balance the books, Dun asked every minister for fiscal proposals.

sentences.zh: 議行二十九事，益纖屑傷大體。

translations.literal: Twenty-nine measures were adopted, ever more petty and harmful to larger principle.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-nine schemes were adopted—petty measures that harmed sound policy.

sentences.zh: 應奎就移戶部，致仕歸，卒。

translations.literal: Yingkui was then moved to the Ministry of Revenue, retired on grounds of age, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui later held the revenue ministry, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 應奎為諫官，屢犯權貴，以風節自厲。

translations.literal: As a remonstrance official Yingkui repeatedly defied powerful men and prided himself on integrity.
translations.idiomatic: As a censor he repeatedly challenged the mighty and held himself to high standards.

sentences.zh: 晚官計曹，一切為茍且計，功名大損於前。

translations.literal: Late in his career at the accounts office he resorted entirely to expedients, and his reputation suffered greatly compared with before.
translations.idiomatic: Late as revenue minister he turned to shabby expedients and his fame fell far below his early years.

sentences.zh: 有與應奎同姓名者，余姚人，字文卿。

translations.literal: There was another man of the same name as Yingkui, from Yuyao, styled Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: Another Sun Yingkui, from Yuyao, courtesy name Wenqing, shared the name.

sentences.zh: 由進士授行人，擢禮科給事中。

translations.literal: Having passed the jinshi he was appointed courier; he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi and courier, he rose to a rites-bureau supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 疏劾汪鋐奸，忤旨下詔獄。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeaching Wang Qian for wickedness, offended the imperial will, and was sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Wang Qian for corruption, angered the throne, and went to prison.

sentences.zh: 已復杖闕下，謫華亭縣丞。

translations.literal: Afterward he was again beaten at court and demoted to assistant magistrate of Huating.
translations.idiomatic: He was beaten at court and demoted to Huating assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 鋐亦罷去。

translations.literal: Qian was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian was dismissed too.

sentences.zh: 兩孫給諫之名，並震於朝廷。

translations.literal: The two Suns' names as remonstrance officials both shook the court.
translations.idiomatic: Both Suns made their names as outspoken censors feared at court.

sentences.zh: 累官右副都御史，總理河道。

translations.literal: After several promotions he became right vice censor-in-chief and director-general of the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right vice censor-in-chief and canal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 逾年罷歸。

translations.literal: A year later he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned after a year.

sentences.zh: 為山東布政時，有創開膠萊河議者，應奎力言不可。

translations.literal: As Shandong administration commissioner, when some proposed opening the Jiao-Lai Canal, Yingkui strongly argued against it.
translations.idiomatic: As Shandong commissioner he firmly opposed plans to open the Jiao-Lai Canal.

sentences.zh: 入覲，與吏部尚書爭官屬賢否，時稱其直。

translations.literal: On a court audience he disputed with the minister of personnel over which subordinates were worthy—at the time he was praised for his bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: At court he argued with the personnel minister over officials' merit and was hailed for his frankness.

sentences.zh: 方鈍，巴陵人。

translations.literal: Fang Dun was a native of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Dun came from Baling.

sentences.zh: 掌戶部七年，廉慎無過。

translations.literal: He held the Ministry of Revenue for seven years, frugal and cautious without fault.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the revenue ministry seven years, thrifty and blameless.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩中之，詔改南京，遂乞骸骨歸。

translations.literal: Yan Song struck at him; by edict he was moved to Nanjing, and he asked to retire on grounds of age and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song undermined him; ordered to Nanjing, he retired home.

sentences.zh: 聶豹，字文蔚，吉安永豐人。

translations.literal: Nie Bao, styled Wenwei, was a native of Yongfeng in Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Bao, courtesy name Wenwei, came from Yongfeng in Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Zhengde 12.

sentences.zh: 除華亭知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Huating.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Huating.

sentences.zh: 浚陂塘，民復業者三千余戶。

translations.literal: He dredged reservoirs and ponds, and more than three thousand households resumed cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged ponds and dykes; over three thousand households returned to farming.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年召拜御史，巡按福建。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing he was summoned and appointed censor, touring and inspecting Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 4 he was recalled as censor to inspect Fujian.

sentences.zh: 出為蘇州知府。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became Suzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 憂歸，補平陽知府。

translations.literal: After mourning he was reassigned as prefect of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was posted to Pingyang prefect.

sentences.zh: 山西頻中寇，民無寧居。

translations.literal: Shanxi was repeatedly raided by bandits and the people had no peace.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits harried Shanxi and the people lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 豹令富民出錢，罪疑者贖，得萬余金，修郭家溝、冷泉、靈石諸關隘，練鄉勇六千守之。

translations.literal: Bao ordered wealthy households to contribute money; doubtful criminal cases could be ransomed, yielding more than ten thousand cash, with which he repaired the passes at Guojia Ditch, Lengquan, and Lingshi and trained six thousand local militia to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: Bao levied the rich and ransomed doubtful cases for over ten thousand taels, rebuilt Guojia Ditch, Lengquan, and Lingshi passes, and drilled six thousand militia.

sentences.zh: 寇卻，廷議以豹為知兵。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, the court judged that Bao understood military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits retreated and the court deemed Bao militarily capable.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉繪、大學士嚴嵩皆薦之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Liu Hui and Grand Secretary Yan Song both recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Liu Hui and Grand Secretary Yan Song recommended him.

sentences.zh: 擢陜西副使，備兵潼關。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of Shaanxi to prepare defenses at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Shaanxi vice commissioner defending Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 大計拾遺，言官論豹在平陽乾沒，大學士夏言亦惡豹，逮下詔獄，落職歸。

translations.literal: At the great review for overlooked talent, remonstrance officials charged that at Pingyang Bao had embezzled funds; Grand Secretary Xia Yan also disliked Bao, and he was arrested, sent to the imperial prison, stripped of office, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: At the talent review censors accused him of embezzlement at Pingyang; Xia Yan opposed him; he was jailed, dismissed, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 二十九年秋，都城被寇。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-ninth year the capital was raided by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of year 29 the capital was attacked.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書徐階，豹知華亭時所取士也，為豹訟冤，言其才可大用。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xu Jie, whom Bao had selected as a scholar when he was magistrate of Huating, pleaded his innocence, saying his talent could be greatly used.
translations.idiomatic: Rites minister Xu Jie—whom Bao had advanced at Huating—petitioned for him, saying his talent deserved high office.

sentences.zh: 立召拜右僉都御史，巡撫順天。

translations.literal: He was immediately summoned and appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 未赴，擢兵部右侍郎，尋轉左。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was promoted to right vice minister of war, and soon transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking up the post he was made right then left vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 仇鸞請調宣、大兵入衛，豹陳四慮，謂宜固守宣、大，宣、大安則京師安。

translations.literal: Qiu Luan requested that troops from Xuanfu and Datong be transferred to guard the capital; Bao set forth four concerns, saying Xuan and Dat should be firmly held—if they were secure, the capital would be secure.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiu Luan asked to bring Xuanfu and Datong troops to defend the capital, Bao urged four objections: hold Xuan and Dat firm, and the capital would be safe.

sentences.zh: 鸞怒。

translations.literal: Luan was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Luan was furious.

sentences.zh: 伺豹過無所得，乃已。

translations.literal: He watched for an occasion when Bao passed by but found nothing, and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to catch Bao out but found no pretext and dropped it.

sentences.zh: 三十一年召翁萬達為兵部尚書，未至，卒，以豹代之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Weng Wanda was summoned as Minister of War; before he arrived he died, and Bao replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 Weng Wanda was summoned as war minister but died en route; Bao took his place.

sentences.zh: 奏上防秋事宜，又請增築京師外城，皆報可。

translations.literal: He memorialized on autumn frontier defense and also asked to build an outer wall around the capital; both were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed autumn defense measures and an outer capital wall; both were approved.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，寇大入山西，覆總兵官李淶軍，大掠二十日而去。

translations.literal: That autumn the bandits raided deeply into Shanxi, destroyed the army of regional commander Li Ze, and after twenty days of great plunder withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn raiders overran Shanxi, crushed commander Li Ze's army, looted for twenty days, and left.

sentences.zh: 總督蘇祐反以大捷聞，為巡按御史毛鵬所發，章下兵部。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Su You instead reported a great victory, which touring censor Mao Peng exposed; the memorial was sent to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Coordinator Su You falsely claimed victory until censor Mao Peng exposed him and the case went to the war ministry.

sentences.zh: 豹言：「寇雖有所掠，而我師斬獲過當，實上玄垂祐，陛下威靈所致。

translations.literal: Bao said: "Though the bandits did some looting, our forces' kills and captures were more than equal—it was truly Heaven's blessing and Your Majesty's majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Bao argued that despite looting, Ming kills exceeded losses—Heaven and the emperor's majesty had prevailed.

sentences.zh: 宜擇吉祭告，論功行賞。

translations.literal: He asked that an auspicious day be chosen for sacrificial announcement and merits rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: He urged a victory rite and rewards.

sentences.zh: 」帝喜。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 進秩任子者數十人，豹亦加太子少保，蔭錦衣世千戶。

translations.literal: Several dozen men were promoted in rank or had sons ennobled; Bao was also made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted a hereditary command in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens were promoted or had sons ennobled; Bao became junior guardian with a hereditary guard command.

sentences.zh: 京師外城成，進太子少傅。

translations.literal: When the outer capital wall was completed, he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the outer wall was finished he was made junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 南北屢奏捷，及類奏諸邊功，豹率歸功玄祐，祭告行賞如初。

translations.literal: Victories were repeatedly reported from north and south, and when frontier merits were summarized by category, Bao again attributed them to Heaven's blessing and ordered sacrifices and rewards as before.
translations.idiomatic: As victories piled up, Bao again credited Heaven, ordered rites, and handed out rewards.

sentences.zh: 豹亦進太子太保。

translations.literal: Bao was also promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 當是時，西北邊數遭寇，東南倭又起，羽書日數至。

translations.literal: At that time the northwest frontier suffered repeated raids and pirates rose in the southeast; urgent dispatches arrived daily.
translations.idiomatic: The northwest was raided repeatedly and southeastern pirates grew; urgent reports arrived daily.

sentences.zh: 豹本無應變才，而大學士嵩與豹鄉里，徐階亦入政府，故豹甚為帝所倚。

translations.literal: Bao had no real talent for crisis, but Grand Secretary Yan Song was his fellow townsman and Xu Jie had also entered government, so the emperor relied on Bao heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Bao lacked crisis skill, but Yan Song was his townsman and Xu Jie was in power, so the emperor leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 久之，寇患日棘，帝深以為憂。

translations.literal: After a long time the bandit threat grew daily worse and the emperor was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: As raids worsened the emperor grew deeply anxious.

sentences.zh: 豹卒無所謀畫，條奏皆具文，帝漸知其短。

translations.literal: Bao still offered no real plans; his memorials were all empty forms, and the emperor gradually knew his shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: Bao produced no real strategy; his papers were hollow, and the emperor saw his limits.

sentences.zh: 會侍郎趙文華陳七事致仕，侍郎朱隆禧請設巡視福建大臣，開海濱互市禁，豹皆格不行。

translations.literal: When Vice Minister Zhao Wenhua memorialized seven matters and retired, and Vice Minister Zhu Longxi asked for a grand coordinator to inspect Fujian and to open coastal mutual-trade bans, Bao blocked them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Wenhua retired on seven proposals and Zhu Longxi urged a Fujian inspector and coastal trade, Bao blocked both.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒切責。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him sharply in anger.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged and rebuked him harshly.

sentences.zh: 豹震懾請罪，復辨增官、開市之非，再下詔譙讓。

translations.literal: Bao, shaken, begged forgiveness and again argued against extra posts and opening trade; the emperor again issued an edict of reproof.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Bao apologized, defended his opposition to new posts and trade, and was rebuked again.

sentences.zh: 豹愈惶懼，條便宜五事以獻。

translations.literal: Bao grew still more fearful and submitted five expedient measures.
translations.idiomatic: More frightened than ever, he offered five practical proposals.

sentences.zh: 帝意終不懌，降俸二級。

translations.literal: The emperor remained displeased and reduced his salary by two grades.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cut his salary two grades.

sentences.zh: 頃之，竟以中旨罷，而用楊博代之。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed by secret edict and Yang Bo replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a secret edict removed him; Yang Bo took his place.

sentences.zh: 歸數年卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: After several years at home he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home several years later, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈少保，謚貞襄。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing he was posthumously made Junior Guardian, with the posthumous title Zhenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In early Longqing he was posthumously made junior guardian with the title Zhenxiang.

sentences.zh: 豹初好王守仁良知之說，與辨難，心益服。

translations.literal: At first Bao favored Wang Shouren's doctrine of innate knowing; after debating with him he became still more convinced.
translations.idiomatic: He first admired Wang Shouren's teaching of innate knowing and, after debate, admired it more.

sentences.zh: 後聞守仁歿，為位哭，以弟子自處。

translations.literal: Later, hearing Shouren had died, he set up a mourning place and wept, comporting himself as a disciple.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouren died he mourned him as a disciple.

sentences.zh: 及系獄，著《困辨錄》，於王守仁說頗有異同雲。

translations.literal: While imprisoned he wrote Records of Hard Distinctions, which differs in places from Wang Shouren's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: In prison he wrote Records of Hard Distinctions, partly diverging from Wang Shouren.

sentences.zh: 李默，字時言，甌寧人。

translations.literal: Li Mo, styled Shiyan, was a native of Ouning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mo, courtesy name Shiyan, came from Ouning.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Zhengde 16.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，改戶部主事，進兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing he was moved to secretary in the Bureau of Revenue and promoted to vice director in the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing he became a revenue secretary, then war vice director.

sentences.zh: 調吏部，歷驗封郎中。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, he served successively as director in the Bureau of Honors.
translations.idiomatic: At the personnel ministry he rose through the honors bureau.

sentences.zh: 真人邵元節貴幸，請封誥，默執不予。

translations.literal: The Daoist master Shao Yuanjie was in favor and asked for patent letters of enfeoffment; Mo firmly withheld them.
translations.idiomatic: Favored Daoist Shao Yuanjie sought ennoblement patents; Mo refused.

sentences.zh: 十一年為武會試同考官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was associate examiner for the military metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he co-examined the military metropolitan exam.

sentences.zh: 及宴兵部，默據賓席，欲坐尚書王憲上。

translations.literal: At the banquet at the Ministry of War, Mo took the guest seat and tried to sit above Minister Wang Xian.
translations.idiomatic: At the war ministry banquet Mo took the guest seat above Minister Wang Xian.

sentences.zh: 憲劾其不遜，謫寧國同知。

translations.literal: Xian impeached him for insubordination and he was demoted to associate prefect of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: Xian impeached him for insolence and he was demoted to Ningguo associate prefect.

sentences.zh: 屢遷浙江左布政使，入為太常卿，掌南京國子監事。

translations.literal: After several promotions he became left administration commissioner of Zhejiang, entered office as vice minister of imperial sacrifices, and directed the National University at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Zhejiang left commissioner, then Nanjing vice minister of sacrifices directing the National University.

sentences.zh: 博士等官得與科道選，自默發之。

translations.literal: That doctors and other officials could be chosen with censors and supervising secretaries began with Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Mo began selecting university doctors alongside censors and supervising secretaries.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部左、右侍郎，代夏邦謨為尚書。

translations.literal: He rose through left and right vice minister of personnel and replaced Xia Bangmo as minister.
translations.idiomatic: He became left and right vice minister, then replaced Xia Bangmo as personnel minister.

sentences.zh: 自正德初焦芳、張彩後，吏部無侍郎拜尚書者。

translations.literal: Since Jiao Fang and Zhang Cai in early Zhengde, no vice minister of personnel had been directly appointed minister.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jiao Fang and Zhang Cai in early Zhengde, no vice minister had jumped straight to minister.

sentences.zh: 默出帝特簡，蓋異數也。

translations.literal: Mo's appointment was a special selection by the emperor—truly an exceptional case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's special choice of Mo was exceptional.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩柄政，擅黜陟權。

translations.literal: Yan Song held power and monopolized appointments and dismissals.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song monopolized appointments.

sentences.zh: 默每持己意，嵩銜之。

translations.literal: Mo often held to his own view, and Song bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Mo often resisted him; Song resented it.

sentences.zh: 會推遼東巡撫，列布政使張臬、謝存儒以上。

translations.literal: When the Liaodong grand coordinator was to be chosen, administration commissioners Zhang Nie and Xie Cunru were listed at the top.
translations.idiomatic: For Liaodong grand coordinator, commissioners Zhang Nie and Xie Cunru topped the list.

sentences.zh: 帝問嵩，嵩言其不任。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Song, and Song said they were unfit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Song, who called them unfit.

sentences.zh: 奪默職為民，以萬鏜代。

translations.literal: Mo was stripped of office and made a commoner; Wan Yong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was dismissed as a commoner; Wan Yong replaced him.

sentences.zh: 默掌銓僅七月。

translations.literal: Mo held the power of appointment only seven months.
translations.idiomatic: He held the seals only seven months.

sentences.zh: 逾年，鏜罷，特旨復用默。

translations.literal: A year later Yong was dismissed and Mo was specially reappointed by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Yong fell and Mo was specially recalled.

sentences.zh: 已，命入直西內，賜直廬，許苑中乘馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to attend in the western inner court, given a lodge, and permitted to ride in the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the western inner court, received lodgings, and rode in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 尋進太子少保。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made junior guardian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復命兼翰林學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was again ordered to serve concurrently as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon also made Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 給事中梁夢龍劾默徇私，帝為責夢龍。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Liang Menglong impeached Mo for favoritism; the emperor rebuked Menglong for Mo's sake.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Menglong charged favoritism; the emperor rebuked Menglong instead.

sentences.zh: 會大計群吏，默戒門下謝賓客，同直大臣亦不得燕見，嵩甚恨。

translations.literal: At the great review of officials Mo warned his staff to refuse guests; even fellow ministers on duty could not visit him casually—Song hated this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: At the general review Mo shut his door to guests, even colleagues—Song hated it.

sentences.zh: 趙文華視師還，默氣折之。

translations.literal: When Zhao Wenhua returned from inspecting troops, Mo humbled himself before him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Wenhua returned from the army Mo deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 總督楊宜罷，嵩、文華欲用胡宗憲，默推王誥代，兩人恨滋甚。

translations.literal: When grand coordinator Yang Yi was dismissed, Song and Wenhua wanted Hu Zongxian; Mo pushed Wang Gao instead, and the two hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yi fell, Song and Wenhua wanted Hu Zongxian; Mo backed Wang Gao, deepening their hatred.

sentences.zh: 初，文華為帝言余倭無幾，而巡按御史周如鬥以敗狀聞。

translations.literal: Earlier Wenhua had told the emperor the remaining pirates were few, yet touring censor Zhou Rudou reported defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua had told the emperor few pirates remained, but censor Zhou Rudou reported defeats.

sentences.zh: 帝疑，數詰嵩。

translations.literal: The emperor was suspicious and repeatedly questioned Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted and pressed Song repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 文華謀所以自解，稔帝喜告訐。

translations.literal: Wenhua sought a way to clear himself, knowing the emperor delighted in accusations.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhua, knowing the emperor welcomed informers, sought an escape.

sentences.zh: 會默試選人策問，言「漢武、唐憲以英睿興盛業，晚節用匪人而敗」，遂奏默誹謗。

translations.literal: When Mo set an examination question for candidates saying "Emperors Wu of Han and Xian of Tang, though brilliant, in their late years used wicked men and failed," he memorialized that Mo had slandered.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's exam question cited Han Wu and Tang Xian failing through wicked late ministers; Wenhua called it slander.

sentences.zh: 且言：「殘寇不難滅，以督撫非人，敗衄。

translations.literal: He also said: "The remnant pirates are not hard to destroy; because the coordinators are unfit, there are defeats."
translations.idiomatic: He added that remnant pirates were easy to crush but bad coordinators caused defeats.

sentences.zh: 由默恨臣劾其同鄉張經，思為報復。

translations.literal: Because Mo resented my impeachment of his fellow townsman Zhang Jing, he sought revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Mo resented my attack on his townsman Zhang Jing and sought revenge.

sentences.zh: 臣論曹邦輔，即嗾給事中夏栻、孫浚媒孽臣。

translations.literal: When I criticized Cao Bangfu, he incited supervising secretaries Xia Shi and Sun Jun to fabricate charges against me.
translations.idiomatic: When I criticized Cao Bangfu he set censors Xia Shi and Sun Jun on me.

sentences.zh: 延今半載，疆事日非。

translations.literal: For half a year since, frontier affairs have worsened daily.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier affairs have worsened for half a year.

sentences.zh: 昨推總督，又不用宗憲而用誥。

translations.literal: Yesterday in choosing a grand coordinator he again refused Zongxian and used Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday he again chose Gao over Zongxian for grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 東南塗炭何時解？

translations.literal: When will the southeast's devastation end?
translations.idiomatic: When will the southeast be saved?

sentences.zh: 陛下宵旰憂何時釋？

translations.literal: When will Your Majesty's nightly anxieties cease?
translations.idiomatic: When will the emperor sleep easy?

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，下禮部及法司議。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and sent the case to the Ministry of Rites and the judiciary for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged and referred the case to rites and the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 奏默偏執自用，失大臣體；

translations.literal: They memorialized that Mo was obstinate and self-willed, unbecoming a chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: They ruled Mo obstinate and unfit for high office;

sentences.zh: 所引漢、唐事，非所宜言。

translations.literal: the Han and Tang examples he cited were not what should be said.
translations.idiomatic: and his Han and Tang examples were improper.

sentences.zh: 帝責禮部尚書王用賓等黨護，各奪俸三月，而下默詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Minister of Rites Wang Yongbin and the others for factional protection, reduced all their salaries three months, and sent Mo to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: He punished rites minister Wang Yongbin and others for shielding Mo, cut their pay three months, and jailed Mo.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書何鰲遂引子罵父律絞。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice He Ao then applied the statute on a son cursing his father and recommended strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Justice minister He Ao applied the son-cursing-father statute and urged strangulation.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「律不著臣罵君，謂必無也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The code does not list a minister cursing his ruler, thinking it could not happen."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said the code had no minister-cursing-ruler clause because none was expected.

sentences.zh: 今有之，其加等斬。

translations.literal: "Now that it has happened, increase the penalty to decapitation."
translations.idiomatic: "Now increase it to decapitation."

sentences.zh: 」錮於獄，默竟瘐死。

translations.literal: Imprisoned, Mo eventually died of illness in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned, Mo died of illness in jail.

sentences.zh: 時三十五年二月也。

translations.literal: It was the second month of the thirty-fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the second month of year 35.

sentences.zh: 默博雅有才辨，以氣自豪。

translations.literal: Mo was learned, elegant, and eloquent, proud in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was learned and eloquent, proud by nature.

sentences.zh: 同考武試，得陸炳為門生。

translations.literal: As associate examiner for the military examination he took Lu Bing as a protégé.
translations.idiomatic: He took Lu Bing as protégé in the military exam.

sentences.zh: 炳貴盛，力推轂。

translations.literal: When Bing rose to power and glory, he pushed Mo forward vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Bing rose he pushed Mo hard.

sentences.zh: 默由外吏驟顯，有所恃，不附嵩。

translations.literal: Mo, suddenly prominent from outside office, had backing and did not attach himself to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly elevated from local office, Mo had backing and refused to follow Song.

sentences.zh: 凡有銓除，與爭可否，氣甚壯。

translations.literal: Whenever there was an appointment he disputed whether it should stand, and his spirit was very bold.
translations.idiomatic: He fought every appointment, boldly and openly.

sentences.zh: 然性褊淺，用愛憎為軒輊，頗私鄉舊，以恩威自歸，士論亦不甚附之。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was narrow and shallow; he weighed men by personal likes and dislikes, favored hometown friends, and sought to win loyalty through kindness and severity—public opinion did not greatly support him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was petty, favored hometown ties, ruled by whim, and won little esteem.

sentences.zh: 默既得罪，繼之者吳鵬、歐陽必進，視嵩父子意，承順惟謹，吏部權盡失。

translations.literal: After Mo's fall, Wu Peng and Ouyang Bijin succeeded him; reading Yan Song and his sons' wishes, they complied carefully, and the Ministry of Personnel lost all power.
translations.idiomatic: After Mo, Wu Peng and Ouyang Bijin obeyed the Songs and the personnel ministry lost all power.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，復默官，予祭葬。

translations.literal: In Longqing his office was restored and sacrificial burial granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing his rank was restored and he received state burial.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，賜謚文湣。

translations.literal: In Wanli he was given the posthumous title Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli he received the posthumous title Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 萬鏜，字仕鳴，進賢人。

translations.literal: Wan Yong, styled Shiming, was a native of Jinxian.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Yong, courtesy name Shiming, came from Jinxian.

sentences.zh: 父福，金華知府。

translations.literal: His father Fu was prefect of Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu was Jinhua prefect.

sentences.zh: 鏜登弘治十八年進士。

translations.literal: Yong passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Hongzhi 18.

sentences.zh: 正德中，由刑部主事屢遷吏部文選郎中。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign, from secretary in the Bureau of Punishments he rose repeatedly to director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde he rose from punishments secretary to appointments director.

sentences.zh: 司署火，下獄，贖還職。

translations.literal: When his office caught fire he was imprisoned and, after ransom, returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When his office burned he was jailed, ransomed, and restored.

sentences.zh: 歷太常、大理少卿。

translations.literal: He served as vice minister of imperial sacrifices and of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice minister of sacrifices and of judicial review.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，以鏜嘗貽書知縣劉源清，令預防宸濠，賚金幣。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded, because Yong had once sent a letter to magistrate Liu Yuanqing urging precautions against Prince of Ning Chen Hao, he was rewarded with gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: On the Jiajing succession Yong was rewarded for warning Liu Yuanqing against the Prince of Ning rebellion.

sentences.zh: 尋遷順天府尹，累遷右副都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to prefect of Shuntian and rose repeatedly to right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He became Shuntian prefect, then right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部侍郎、右都御史，皆南京。

translations.literal: He served as vice minister of war and right censor-in-chief, all at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He held Nanjing posts as war vice minister and right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 彗星見，應詔陳八事。

translations.literal: When a comet appeared he responded to an edict with eight proposals.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared he memorialized eight reforms.

sentences.zh: 中言：「人邪正相懸，而形跡易混。

translations.literal: Among them he said: "The upright and the wicked are far apart, yet their outward signs are easily confused."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote that good and evil look alike outwardly.

sentences.zh: 其大較有四：人主所取於下者，曰任怨，曰任事，曰恭順，曰無私；

translations.literal: Broadly there are four points: what the ruler wants in subordinates is said to be willingness to bear blame, ability to handle affairs, deference, and selflessness;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler wants subordinates who bear blame, get things done, defer, and stay selfless;

sentences.zh: 而邪臣之恣強戾、好紛更、巧逢迎、肆攻訐者，其跡似之。

translations.literal: yet wicked ministers who are overbearing, fond of needless change, skilled at flattery, and free with attacks—their traces resemble these.
translations.idiomatic: yet wicked men who are domineering, restless, flattering, and vicious look the same.

sentences.zh: 人主所惡於下者，曰避事，曰沽名，曰朋黨，曰矯激；

translations.literal: What the ruler hates in subordinates is said to be shirking duty, courting reputation, forming factions, and affected austerity;
translations.idiomatic: What the ruler hates is shirking, grandstanding, faction, and showy austerity;

sentences.zh: 而正臣之守成法、恤公議、體群情、規君失者，其跡似之。

translations.literal: yet upright ministers who uphold established law, heed public opinion, consider the feelings of the multitude, and admonish the ruler's faults—their traces resemble these.
translations.idiomatic: yet honest men who uphold law, heed public opinion, and remonstrate look the same outwardly.

sentences.zh: 察之不精，則邪正倒置，而國是亂矣，此不可不慎也。

translations.literal: If one does not examine finely, wicked and upright are inverted and state policy is thrown into confusion—this must not be treated carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Without careful judgment good and evil reverse and policy collapses—this demands caution.

sentences.zh: 治天下貴實不貴文。

translations.literal: In governing the realm substance is prized, not ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Governing the realm values substance over show.

sentences.zh: 今陛下議禮制度考文，至明備矣，而於理財用人安民講武之道，或有缺焉。

translations.literal: Today Your Majesty's discussion of ritual, institutions, and textual study is brilliantly complete, yet in managing finances, employing men, settling the people, and military preparedness there may be gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and scholarship are thorough, yet finance, appointments, welfare, and defense may still lack.

sentences.zh: 願輟聲容之繁飾，略太平之美觀，而專從事於實用，斯治天下之道得矣。

translations.literal: I beg that Your Majesty set aside elaborate display and the beautiful spectacle of great peace and devote yourself wholly to practical use—then the way to govern the realm will be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Set aside pageantry and pursue practical governance—that is the true way to rule.

sentences.zh: 至大禮大獄得罪諸臣，幽錮已久，乞量加寬錄。

translations.literal: As for the ministers condemned in the Great Rites and Great Prison cases, long confined in secret, I beg that they be measured for lenient restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers long imprisoned after the Great Rites and Great Prison cases deserve measured amnesty.

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，斥為民，令吏部錮勿用。

translations.literal: " The emperor was furious, dismissed him as a commoner, and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to imprison his name and not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, made him a commoner, and barred the personnel ministry from using him.

sentences.zh: 家居十年，屢推薦，輒報罷。

translations.literal: At home for ten years he was repeatedly recommended, but each time the reply was dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years at home every recommendation was rejected.

sentences.zh: 同年生嚴嵩柄政，援引之。

translations.literal: His fellow jinshi Yan Song held power and brought him forward.
translations.idiomatic: Classmate Yan Song in power pulled him back in.

sentences.zh: 湖廣蠟爾山蠻叛，起鏜副都御史，相機剿撫。

translations.literal: When the Laer Mountain Miao of Huguang rebelled, Yong was raised to vice censor-in-chief to suppress or pacify as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang's Laer Mountain Miao rebelled; Yong was made vice censor-in-chief to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 鏜納土指揮田應朝策，誘致其酋，督兵破之。

translations.literal: Yong accepted the stratagem of native commander Tian Yingchao, lured the chieftains in, and supervised troops to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Yong used native commander Tian Yingchao's plan to lure and crush the chiefs.

sentences.zh: 條上善後七事，帝鹹報可。

translations.literal: He listed seven follow-up measures; the emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: Seven follow-up measures were approved.

sentences.zh: 召鏜還。

translations.literal: Yong was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，銅平酋龍子賢復叛，御史繆文龍言鏜剿撫皆失。

translations.literal: Before long the chieftain Long Zixian of Tongping rebelled again; censor Miu Wenlong said Yong had failed in both suppression and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tongping chief Long Zixian rebelled again; censor Miu Wenlong blamed Yong's failure.

sentences.zh: 詔下撫按官勘覆，歸罪於參將李經，事乃解。

translations.literal: An edict ordered grand coordinator and touring inspector to investigate; guilt was placed on regional commander Li Jing and the matter was closed.
translations.idiomatic: Investigators blamed regional commander Li Jing and closed the case.

sentences.zh: 鏜得為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Yong was able to become vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Yong became vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 遷南京刑、禮二部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of justice and of rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He became Nanjing minister of justice and of rites.

sentences.zh: 召掌刑部。

translations.literal: He was summoned to head the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to head justice.

sentences.zh: 俄代李默為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Li Mo as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He soon replaced Li Mo as personnel minister.

sentences.zh: 鏜既為嵩所引，每事委隨，又頗通饋遺。

translations.literal: Once Yong had been brought in by Song, he deferred to him in every matter and also rather freely exchanged gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Raised by Song, he deferred on everything and traded gifts freely.

sentences.zh: 撫治鄖陽都御史闕，鏜以通政使趙文華名上。

translations.literal: When the post of grand coordinator of Fuyang was vacant, Yong listed Commissioner of Transmission Zhao Wenhua at the top.
translations.idiomatic: For Fuyang grand coordinator Yong ranked Zhao Wenhua first.

sentences.zh: 會給事中朱伯辰劾文華，文華上言：「納言之職，例不外推。

translations.literal: When supervising secretary Zhu Bochen impeached Wenhua, Wenhua memorialized: "The duty of remonstrance is by precedent not to be farmed out."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bochen impeached Wenhua, who replied that remonstrance should not be outsourced.

sentences.zh: 鏜意在出臣，又嗾所親伯辰論劾，欲去臣。

translations.literal: "Yong meant to drive me out and incited his intimate Bochen to impeach me, wishing to remove me."
translations.idiomatic: "Yong meant to oust me and incited Bochen to attack me."

sentences.zh: 且鏜以侍郎起用，乃朦朧奏二品九年滿，得加太子少保。

translations.literal: "Moreover Yong, raised from vice minister, vaguely memorialized that nine years at the second rank were complete and obtained Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent."
translations.idiomatic: "Raised from vice minister, he vaguely claimed nine years at second rank for junior guardian."

sentences.zh: 又以不得一品，面謾腹誹，無大臣禮。

translations.literal: "Again, because he did not obtain the first rank, he mocked to the face and slandered in the heart—without the decorum of a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: "Denied first rank, he mocked openly and slandered privately—no minister's decorum."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，遂與伯辰並黜為民。

translations.literal: " The emperor was angry and dismissed both him and Bochen as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Yong and Bochen as commoners.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died years later.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing his office was restored and he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In early Longqing his rank was restored and he was posthumously made grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 周延，字南喬，吉水人。

translations.literal: Zhou Yan, styled Nanqiao, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yan, courtesy name Nanqiao, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Jiajing 2.

sentences.zh: 除潛江知縣，改新會，擢兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Qianjiang, transferred to Xinhui, and promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was magistrate of Qianjiang and Xinhui, then war-bureau supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 時議新建伯王守仁罪，將奪其爵。

translations.literal: At the time it was debated that Marquis of Xinjian Wang Shouren was guilty and his title would be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Court debated stripping Marquis Wang Shouren of his title.

sentences.zh: 延抗疏為訟，坐謫太倉州判官。

translations.literal: Yan memorialized strongly in his defense and was demoted to assistant magistrate of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: He defended Wang in a strong memorial and was demoted to Taicang assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 歷南京吏部郎中，出為廣東參政。

translations.literal: He rose through director in the Ministry of Personnel at Nanjing and went out as administration commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Nanjing personnel director, then Guangdong administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 撫安南，征黎寇，皆預，有功。

translations.literal: In pacifying Annam and campaigning against Li bandits he took part and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Annam and fight Li rebels with merit.

sentences.zh: 三遷廣東左布政使。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became left administration commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted thrice he became left commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 以右副都御史巡撫應天。

translations.literal: He was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: He became right vice censor-in-chief and Yingtian grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 靖海寇林成亂。

translations.literal: He quelled the sea-bandit Lin Cheng's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He quelled sea-bandit Lin Cheng.

sentences.zh: 進兵部右侍郎，提督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right vice minister of war and director-general of military affairs in the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He became right vice war minister and two-Guang military director.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as left vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as left vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 歷南京右都御史，吏、兵二部尚書。

translations.literal: He served as right censor-in-chief at Nanjing and minister of personnel and of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was Nanjing right censor-in-chief, then personnel and war minister.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十四年召為左都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Jiajing he was summoned as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 34 he was summoned as left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 帝用給事中徐浦議，令廷臣及督撫各舉邊才。

translations.literal: The emperor, adopting supervising secretary Xu Pu's proposal, ordered court ministers and grand coordinators each to recommend frontier talent.
translations.idiomatic: On Xu Pu's proposal the emperor ordered frontier talent recommendations.

sentences.zh: 於是故侍郎郭宗臯，都御史曹邦輔、吳嶽，祭酒鄒守益，修撰羅洪先，御史吳悌、方涯，主事唐樞，參政周大禮、曹亨，參議劉誌，知府黃華在舉中。

translations.literal: Thereupon former vice minister Guo Zonggao, censors-in-chief Cao Bangfu and Wu Yue, libationer Zou Shouyi, compiler Luo Hongxian, censors Wu Ti and Fang Ya, director Tang Shu, administration commissioners Zhou Dali and Cao Heng, administration vice commissioner Liu Zhi, and prefect Huang Huazai were among those nominated.
translations.idiomatic: Former vice minister Guo Zonggao, censors Cao Bangfu and Wu Yue, Zou Shouyi, Luo Hongxian, and others were nominated.

sentences.zh: 御史羅廷唯駁曰：「浦疏本言邊才，而今廷臣乃以清修、苦節、實學、懿行舉，去初議遠矣。

translations.literal: Censor Luo Tingwei objected: "Pu's memorial spoke of frontier talent, yet court ministers now nominate men for pure conduct, bitter integrity, solid learning, and fine conduct—far from the original proposal."
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tingwei objected that nominees were scholars of virtue, not frontier fighters.

sentences.zh: 況又有夤緣進者。

translations.literal: Moreover there are those who advance by pull.
translations.idiomatic: Some nominees had pulled strings.

sentences.zh: 是假明詔開幸門。

translations.literal: This uses a clear edict to open a gate of favor.
translations.idiomatic: That abuses the edict to open patronage.

sentences.zh: 」帝納其言，責吏部濫舉，命與都察院更議。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his view, rebuked the Ministry of Personnel for careless nomination, and ordered reconsideration with the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, rebuked personnel for sloppy lists, and ordered a redo with the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 延與尚書吳鵬等言所舉皆人望，公無私。

translations.literal: Yan and Minister Wu Peng and others said those nominated were all men of public esteem without private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Wu Peng insisted the nominees were worthy and impartial.

sentences.zh: 帝終不悅，切責延等，而舉者悉報罷。

translations.literal: The emperor remained displeased, sharply rebuked Yan and the others, and all nominees were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remained angry, rebuked Yan, and rejected every nominee.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，海內賢士大夫被斥者眾，及是舉上，稍冀復用，而為廷唯所阻，自是皆不復召矣。

translations.literal: In Shizong's time many worthy scholars were banished; at this nomination there was slight hope of reuse, but Tingwei blocked it—after that none were recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Many banished scholars hoped for recall; Tingwei's block ended that hope.

sentences.zh: 延顏面寒峭，砥節奉公。

translations.literal: Yan's face was stern and cold; he upheld integrity in serving the public.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was stern-faced and incorruptible in office.

sentences.zh: 權臣用事，政以賄成，延未嘗有染。

translations.literal: When powerful ministers held sway and government ran on bribes, Yan was never tainted.
translations.idiomatic: When power sold offices Yan took no bribes.

sentences.zh: 然居臺端七年，無諫諍名。

translations.literal: Yet in seven years at the head of the Censorate he won no fame for remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet seven years as censor-in-chief brought no fame for speaking out.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈太子太保，謚簡肅。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Jiansu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office, posthumously grand guardian with the title Jiansu.

sentences.zh: 延卒，歐陽必進代。

translations.literal: After Yan died, Ouyang Bijin replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Bijin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 逾月，遷吏部，乃以潘恩繼之。

translations.literal: A month later he was moved to the Ministry of Personnel, and Pan En succeeded at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he went to personnel and Pan En took the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 恩，字子仁，上海人。

translations.literal: En, styled Ziren, was a native of Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Pan En, courtesy name Ziren, came from Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Jiajing 2.

sentences.zh: 授祁州知州，調繁鈞州。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Qizhou and transferred to the demanding post of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was prefect of Qizhou, then busy Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 鈞，徽王封國也，宗戚豪悍，恩約束之。

translations.literal: Jun was the enfeoffment of the Prince of Hui; clansmen and the powerful were fierce, and En restrained them.
translations.idiomatic: At Prince of Hui's Junzhou En restrained violent kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 擢南京刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He became Nanjing justice vice director.

sentences.zh: 遷廣西提學僉事，署按察使事。

translations.literal: He was moved to education intendant of Guangxi and acted as provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became Guangxi education intendant acting surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 有大猾匿靖江王所，捕之急，王不得已出之。

translations.literal: A great villain hid in the Prince of Jingjiang's residence; when pursuit was urgent the prince had no choice but to hand him over.
translations.idiomatic: A great rogue hid with Prince of Jingjiang and was surrendered under pressure.

sentences.zh: 憾恩，誣以事，按無實得免。

translations.literal: The prince resented En and falsely charged him, but investigation found no truth and he was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The prince framed him; inquiry found nothing and he was cleared.

sentences.zh: 累遷山東副使。

translations.literal: After several promotions he became vice commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Shandong vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 御史葉經以試錄忤旨，並恩下詔獄，謫廣東河源典史。

translations.literal: Censor Ye Jing offended the imperial will over the examination record and both he and En were sent to the imperial prison; En was demoted to recorder of Heyuan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ye Jing offended the throne; En was jailed and demoted to Heyuan recorder.

sentences.zh: 四遷，復為江西副使，進浙江左參政。

translations.literal: After four promotions he again became vice commissioner of Jiangxi and advanced to left administration commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Restored through four promotions, he became Jiangxi vice commissioner then Zhejiang left commissioner.

sentences.zh: 按部海鹽，倭猝至，圍城數匝。

translations.literal: While inspecting Haiyan, pirates suddenly arrived and surrounded the city many layers deep.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting Haiyan, he was besieged by sudden pirate attack.

sentences.zh: 恩與參將湯克寬、僉事姜頤力禦卻之。

translations.literal: En, with regional commander Tang Kekuan and intendant Jiang Yi, defended strenuously and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: With Tang Kekuan and Jiang Yi he defended and repelled them.

sentences.zh: 俄遷浙江左布政使，以右副都御史巡撫河南。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to left administration commissioner of Zhejiang and made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He became Zhejiang left commissioner, then Henan grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 偕按臣劾徽王載埨貪虐，遂奪國。

translations.literal: Together with the touring inspector he impeached the Prince of Hui's heir Zaijun for greed and cruelty and stripped the fief.
translations.idiomatic: He and the inspector impeached Prince of Hui heir Zaijun and stripped the fief.

sentences.zh: 伊王典礻英驕橫，恩一切裁之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi's heir Dian Ying was arrogant and overbearing; En curbed him in everything.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yi heir Dian Ying was overbearing; En reined him in.

sentences.zh: 河南民素苦藩府，恩制兩悍王，名大著。

translations.literal: The people of Henan had long suffered from princely estates; En controlled two fierce princes and his fame grew great.
translations.idiomatic: Henan people suffered princely estates; En tamed two fierce princes and became famous.

sentences.zh: 久之，由刑部尚書改左都御史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was moved from Minister of Justice to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from justice minister to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 子允端，為刑部主事。

translations.literal: His son Yunduan was a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yunduan was a justice secretary.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書郭樸，恩門生也，調之禮部。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Guo Pu, En's student, transferred him to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel minister Guo Pu, his student, moved Yunduan to rites.

sentences.zh: 給事中張益劾允端奔兢，恩溺愛，樸徇私。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Zhang Yi impeached Yunduan for frantic ambition; En doted on him and Pu showed favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi charged Yunduan's ambition; En favored him and Pu bent rules.

sentences.zh: 帝置樸不問，改允端南京工部，令恩致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor set Pu aside from inquiry, moved Yunduan to the Ministry of Works at Nanjing, and ordered En to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Pu escaped blame; Yunduan went to Nanjing works and En retired.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，賜存問。

translations.literal: Early in Wanli he was granted imperial inquiry after retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli he received an imperial visit in retirement.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十七。

translations.literal: He died aged eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚恭定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Gongding.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously junior guardian with the title Gongding.

sentences.zh: 賈應春，字東陽，真定人。

translations.literal: Jia Yingchun, styled Dongyang, was a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yingchun, courtesy name Dongyang, came from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Jiajing 2.

sentences.zh: 授南陽知縣，遷和州知州。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Nanyang and transferred to prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was Nanyang magistrate, then Hezhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He entered office as director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He became a justice director.

sentences.zh: 歷知潞安、開封二府。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Lu'an and Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Lu'an and Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 遷陜西副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Shaanxi vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未赴，河南巡按陳蕙劾其貪濫，謫山東鹽運同知，蕙亦坐貶。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, Henan touring inspector Chen Hui impeached him for greed and excess; he was demoted to salt transport associate prefect of Shandong, and Hui was also demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking office Chen Hui impeached him for corruption; he was demoted to Shandong salt associate prefect and Hui too was punished.

sentences.zh: 久之，由漢陽知府復遷陜西副使，進右參政。

translations.literal: After a long time, from prefect of Hanyang he was again promoted to vice commissioner of Shaanxi and advanced to right administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Later, from Hanyang prefect he returned as Shaanxi vice commissioner then right administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 寧羌賊起，會兵討平之。

translations.literal: When bandits rose at Ningqiang, he joined forces to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: He helped crush Ningqiang bandits.

sentences.zh: 遷按察使，左、右布政使，皆在陜西。

translations.literal: He was moved to surveillance commissioner and left and right administration commissioner, all in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became Shaanxi surveillance commissioner and left and right administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 就拜右副都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of that region.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Shaanxi grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 三十二年進兵部右侍郎，總督三邊軍務。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was promoted to right vice minister of war and director-general of military affairs on the three frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 he became right vice war minister and three-frontier director-general.

sentences.zh: 俺答諸部歲擾邊，應春言：「諸邊間諜不通，每寇入莫測其向，我則無所不備。

translations.literal: Altan's tribes raided the frontier yearly; Yingchun said: "On the frontiers spies do not communicate; whenever bandits enter we cannot foresee their direction, while we must prepare everywhere."
translations.idiomatic: Yingchun said frontier spies failed: enemies struck unpredictably while Ming forces spread thin everywhere.

sentences.zh: 兵分勢孤，往往失事。

translations.literal: When troops are divided strength is isolated and affairs are often lost.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered troops often lose.

sentences.zh: 夫寇將內犯，必聚眾治器，臘肉飼馬，傳箭祭旗，其形先露。

translations.literal: When bandits are about to invade inland they must gather crowds, prepare weapons, cure meat and feed horses, and pass arrows and raise banners—their form is revealed first.
translations.idiomatic: Before raiding, enemies gather, arm, salt meat, feed horses, and signal—their signs show first.

sentences.zh: 而我民被掠者，間亦臨邊傳報，頗有左驗。

translations.literal: Yet our people who are plundered also sometimes report at the border with some corroboration.
translations.idiomatic: Plundered civilians sometimes bring corroborating border reports.

sentences.zh: 使邊臣厚以官賞，令密偵候，視漫然散守者，功相十百。

translations.literal: If frontier officials are richly rewarded with office and bounty to order secret reconnaissance, compared with guards scattered at random the merit is ten or a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: Rich rewards for frontier spies would beat scattered garrison duty tenfold.

sentences.zh: 」乃定賞格以請。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he fixed reward regulations and requested approval.
translations.idiomatic: He set spy reward rules and sought approval.

sentences.zh: 帝立從之。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved at once.

sentences.zh: 其秋，寇大入延綏，殺掠五千余人。

translations.literal: That autumn the bandits raided deeply into Yan-sui and killed and plundered more than five thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn raiders killed over five thousand in Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 應春督諸將邀擊，獲首功二百四十，以捷聞。

translations.literal: Yingchun supervised the generals in intercepting attack and obtained two hundred forty heads; he reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: He led intercepts, took 240 heads, and reported victory.

sentences.zh: 而巡按御史吉澄極言敗狀。

translations.literal: Yet touring censor Ji Cheng spoke at length of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Ji Cheng reported defeat instead.

sentences.zh: 帝竟錄應春功，官其一子。

translations.literal: The emperor still recorded Yingchun's merit and ennobled one son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still rewarded Yingchun and ennobled a son.

sentences.zh: 明年罷宣、大總督蘇祐，以應春代。

translations.literal: The next year grand coordinator of Xuan and Dat Su You was dismissed and Yingchun replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he replaced Su You as Xuan-Dat grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 時秋防將屆，代應春者江東未至，令仍舊任。

translations.literal: As autumn defense was due and Jiang Dong, who was to replace Yingchun, had not arrived, he was ordered to remain in his old post.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Dong had not arrived for autumn defense, so Yingchun stayed on.

sentences.zh: 套寇數萬人屯寧夏山後，先遣騎五百余入掠。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of Tatar bandits camped behind Ningxia Mountain and first sent more than five hundred horsemen to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands camped behind Ningxia Mountain and sent 500 raiders first.

sentences.zh: 總兵官姜應熊守紅井以綴敵，而密遣精兵薄其營，斬首百四十余級，進應春右都御史。

translations.literal: Regional commander Jiang Yingxiong held Hongjing to delay the enemy while secretly sending picked troops against their camp, taking more than one hundred forty heads; Yingchun was promoted to right censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yingxiong held Hongjing while elite troops struck the camp for 140 heads; Yingchun was promoted.

sentences.zh: 逾月，寇別部入永昌、西寧，為守將所破。

translations.literal: A month later another band of bandits entered Yongchang and Xining and were defeated by the garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Another band hit Yongchang and Xining and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 番人入鎮羌，總兵官王繼祖擊敗之，並賜應春銀幣。

translations.literal: Tibetans entered Zhenqiang; regional commander Wang Jizu defeated them, and Yingchun too was given gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetans at Zhenqiang were beaten; Yingchun received rewards.

sentences.zh: 久之，寇五千騎犯環慶，為都督袁正所破，掠莊涼，守將邀斬百二十人，再予應春一子官。

translations.literal: After a long time five thousand bandit horsemen raided Huanqing and were broken by Commander Yuan Zheng; plundering Zhuangliang, garrison commanders intercepted and beheaded one hundred twenty men, and Yingchun was again granted one son's office.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand raiders hit Huanqing; intercepts took 120 heads and another son was ennobled.

sentences.zh: 在鎮數載，築邊垣萬一千八百余丈，以花馬池閑田二萬頃給軍屯墾，邊人賴之。

translations.literal: In several years on the frontier he built more than eleven thousand eight hundred zhang of border wall and allotted twenty thousand mu of idle land at Huamachi to military colonies—the frontier people relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: He built 11,800+ zhang of wall and gave 20,000 mu at Huamachi to garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 征拜南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Nanjing revenue minister.

sentences.zh: 論邊垣功，進秩一等。

translations.literal: For border-wall merit his rank was raised one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Border-wall merit raised his rank one grade.

sentences.zh: 旋召為刑部尚書，改戶部。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Minister of Justice and moved to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He became justice minister, then revenue minister.

sentences.zh: 國用不足，應春以為言。

translations.literal: State revenue was insufficient and Yingchun spoke on it.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke on insufficient revenue.

sentences.zh: 因命征不及七分者，所司毋遷官。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was ordered that where collection did not reach seven-tenths, the responsible offices should not promote officials.
translations.idiomatic: Where tax collection fell below seventy percent, no promotions were allowed.

sentences.zh: 漕政廢弛，運艘多逋負，亦以應春言重其罰。

translations.literal: Transport administration was lax and transport ships often defaulted on payments—on Yingchun's word the penalties were also increased.
translations.idiomatic: Transport defaults drew heavier penalties on his advice.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，致仕去。

translations.literal: After more than a year he retired on grounds of age.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 張永明，字鐘誠，烏程人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongming, styled Zhongcheng, was a native of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongming, courtesy name Zhongcheng, came from Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Jiajing 14.

sentences.zh: 除蕪湖知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Wuhu magistrate.

sentences.zh: 獻皇后梓宮南祔，所過繁費不貲。

translations.literal: When the empress's coffin was escorted south for joint burial the expenses along the route were enormous.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's southern burial procession cost enormously.

sentences.zh: 永明堊江岸佛舍為殿，供器飾箔金，財用大省。

translations.literal: Yongming whitewashed riverside Buddhist halls into a palace hall, with vessels and ornaments gilt in leaf gold, and expenses were greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He converted Buddhist halls into a mourning hall with gilt fittings and saved vast expense.

sentences.zh: 尋擢南京刑科給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He became Nanjing punishments supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 寇入大同，山西總督樊繼祖，巡撫史道、陳講等不能禦，永明偕同官論其罪。

translations.literal: When bandits entered Datong, Shanxi grand coordinator Fan Jizu and grand coordinators Shi Dao and Chen Jiang and others could not defend; Yongming with colleagues indicted their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Datong fell he indicted Fan Jizu, Shi Dao, and Chen Jiang.

sentences.zh: 已，又劾兵部尚書張瓚黷貨誤國，又劾大學士嚴嵩及子世蕃貪汙狀。

translations.literal: Later he also impeached Minister of War Zhang Zan for corrupt goods and harming the state, and Grand Secretary Yan Song and his son Shifan for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Zhang Zan and Yan Song and Shifan for corruption.

sentences.zh: 已，又劾兵部尚書戴金為御史巡鹽時，增余鹽羨銀，阻壞邊計。

translations.literal: Later he also impeached Minister of War Dai Jin for increasing surplus-salt silver while touring salt as censor and obstructing frontier plans.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Dai Jin for surplus-salt graft harming frontier policy.

sentences.zh: 疏雖不盡行，中外憚之。

translations.literal: Though the memorials were not fully carried out, inside and outside court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Not all charges stuck, but court and country feared him.

sentences.zh: 出為江西參議。

translations.literal: He went out as administration commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became Jiangxi administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷雲南副使，山西左布政使。
