translations.literal: After several promotions he became vice commissioner of Yunnan and left administration commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Yunnan vice commissioner and Shanxi left commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以右副都御史巡撫河南。

translations.literal: He was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He became Henan grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 伊王典礻英恣橫，永明發其惡，後竟伏辜。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi's heir Dian Ying was willful and overbearing; Yongming exposed his wickedness and in the end he was punished.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed Prince of Yi heir Dian Ying, who was eventually punished.

sentences.zh: 四十年遷刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was moved to right vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In year 40 he became right vice justice minister.

sentences.zh: 未上，改吏部，進左。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was moved to the Ministry of Personnel and advanced to the left.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking office he became left personnel vice minister.

sentences.zh: 尋拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became justice minister.

sentences.zh: 居數月，改左都御史。

translations.literal: After several months he was moved to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he became left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 條上飭歷撫按六事。

translations.literal: He listed six matters for tightening touring grand coordinators and inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed six reforms for touring officials.

sentences.zh: 御史黃廷聘按浙歸，道湘潭，慢知縣陳安。

translations.literal: Censor Huang Tingpin toured Zhejiang on his return and passed Xiangtan, treating magistrate Chen An with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Huang Tingpin insulted Xiangtan magistrate Chen An.

sentences.zh: 安發其裝，得所攜金銀貨幣。

translations.literal: An searched his luggage and found gold, silver, and goods he carried.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An searched his baggage and found gold and goods.

sentences.zh: 廷聘皇恐謝，乃還之。

translations.literal: Tingpin was terrified and apologized, and then returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Tingpin apologized and returned them.

sentences.zh: 永明聞，劾罷廷聘。

translations.literal: When Yongming heard, he impeached and dismissed Tingpin.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming impeached and dismissed Tingpin.

sentences.zh: 浙江參政劉應箕先為廷聘論罷，見廷聘敗，摭其陰事自辨。

translations.literal: Zhejiang administration vice commissioner Liu Yingji had earlier been dismissed on Tingpin's impeachment; seeing Tingpin's fall, he gathered secret matters to plead his own case.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yingji, once dismissed by Tingpin, now defended himself with secret charges.

sentences.zh: 永明惡之，劾應箕，亦斥。

translations.literal: Yongming hated this and impeached Yingji, who was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming impeached Yingji and removed him too.

sentences.zh: 故事，京官考滿，自翰林外皆報名都察院，修庭謁禮。

translations.literal: By precedent, when capital officials finished their term, except for Hanlin all reported their names to the Censorate and performed courtyard audience ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials except Hanlin once reported to the Censorate for courtyard audience.

sentences.zh: 後吏部郎恃權，張濂廢報名，陸光祖廢庭謁。

translations.literal: Later personnel bureau directors relied on power; Zhang Lian abolished name-reporting and Lu Guangzu abolished courtyard audience.
translations.idiomatic: Later directors Zhang Lian and Lu Guangzu ended those rituals.

sentences.zh: 永明榜令遵故事，列儀節奏聞，詔諸司遵守。

translations.literal: Yongming posted an order to follow the old story, set out the ritual steps, and memorialized; an edict ordered all offices to obey.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the rituals by edict.

sentences.zh: 郎中羅良當考滿，先詣永明邸，約免報名庭謁乃過院。

translations.literal: Director Luo Liang, when his term was complete, first went to Yongming's residence and agreed to skip name-reporting and courtyard audience before passing the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Director Luo Liang tried to skip rituals after lobbying Yongming.

sentences.zh: 永明怒，疏言：「此禮行百年，非臣所能損益。

translations.literal: Yongming was angry and memorialized: "This ritual has been practiced a hundred years—not something I can lightly change."
translations.idiomatic: Yongming angrily defended century-old ritual.

sentences.zh: 良輕薄無狀，當罷。

translations.literal: "Liang is frivolous and unseemly and should be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: "Liang is unworthy and should go."

sentences.zh: 又卿貳大臣考滿，詣吏部與堂官相見訖，即詣四司門揖，司官輒南面答揖，亦非禮，當改正。

translations.literal: "Moreover when chief and deputy ministers finish their term, after meeting the ministry chief at the Ministry of Personnel they immediately go to the four bureaus' doors to bow, and bureau officials then reply with a south-facing bow—this too is not ritual and should be corrected."
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked ministers bowing to bureau clerks who bowed back facing south.

sentences.zh: 」良疏辨，奪俸。

translations.literal: Liang memorialized in defense and lost salary.
translations.idiomatic: Liang lost salary in reply.

sentences.zh: 詔禮部會禮科議之，奏言：「永明議是。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to meet with the remonstrance bureau to deliberate; they memorialized: "Yongming's view is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Rites and remonstrance bureau backed Yongming.

sentences.zh: 自今吏部郎其承舊制。

translations.literal: "From now on personnel bureau directors should follow the old system."
translations.idiomatic: Personnel directors must follow old ritual.

sentences.zh: 九卿翰林官揖四司，當罷。

translations.literal: "Nine ministers and Hanlin officials bowing to the four bureaus should cease."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers must not bow to bureau clerks.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 永明素清謹。

translations.literal: Yongming was always pure and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming was pure and careful.

sentences.zh: 掌憲在嚴嵩罷後，以整飭綱維為己任。

translations.literal: Holding the censorate after Yan Song's fall, he took restoring discipline as his duty.
translations.idiomatic: After Song fell he restored censorial discipline.

sentences.zh: 會給事中魏時亮劾，永明力求去，詔許馳驛歸。

translations.literal: When supervising secretary Wei Shiliang impeached him, Yongming strove to leave office and an edict allowed him to return home by relay.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shiliang impeached him; he retired by relay.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next year.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚莊僖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhuangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously junior guardian with the title Zhuangxi.

sentences.zh: 胡松，字汝茂，滁人。

translations.literal: Hu Song, styled Ruma, was a native of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Song, courtesy name Ruma, came from Chu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼嗜學，嘗輯古名臣章奏，慨然有用世誌。

translations.literal: From childhood he loved learning; he once compiled memorials of famous ministers of old and sighed with the will to serve the age.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled ancient ministers' memorials and burned to serve.

sentences.zh: 登嘉靖八年進士，知東平州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Jiajing and was appointed prefect of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Jiajing 8 and governed Dongping.

sentences.zh: 設方略捕盜，民賴以安。

translations.literal: He set stratagems to capture bandits and the people relied on him for peace.
translations.idiomatic: His bandit-catching plans brought peace.

sentences.zh: 再遷南京禮部郎中，歷山西提學副使。

translations.literal: After two promotions he became director in the Ministry of Rites at Nanjing and served as education vice commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became Nanjing rites director then Shanxi education vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十年秋，上邊務十二事，謂：

translations.literal: In the thirtieth autumn he submitted twelve frontier matters, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of year 30 he submitted twelve frontier proposals:

sentences.zh: 去秋俺答掠興、嵐，即傳箭征兵，克期深入。

translations.literal: Last autumn Altan raided Xing and Lan and passed arrows to summon troops, fixing a date for deep invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Last autumn Altan raided Xing-Lan and summoned troops for deep invasion.

sentences.zh: 守臣皆諗聞之。

translations.literal: The defending officials all heard of it in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Defenders knew in advance.

sentences.zh: 而巡撫史道、總兵官王陛等備禦無素。

translations.literal: Yet grand coordinator Shi Dao, regional commander Wang Bi, and others were unprepared by habit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shi Dao and Wang Bi were habitually unprepared.

sentences.zh: 待其壓境，始以求貢上聞。

translations.literal: When the enemy pressed the border they only then memorialized seeking tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Only when raiders arrived did they seek tribute by memorial.

sentences.zh: 又陰致賄遺，令勿侵己分地，冀嫁禍他境。

translations.literal: They also secretly sent bribes, asking that their own districts not be invaded, hoping to shift disaster to other regions.
translations.idiomatic: They bribed enemies to spare their own districts and harm others.

sentences.zh: 今山西之禍，實大同貽之。

translations.literal: Today Shanxi's disaster was truly bequeathed by Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi's disaster came from Datong's failure.

sentences.zh: 宜亟置重典，以厲諸鎮。

translations.literal: Heavy punishment should quickly be set to warn all garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy punishment must warn all frontiers.

sentences.zh: 大同自兵變以來，壯士多逃漠北為寇用，今宜招使歸。

translations.literal: Since the mutiny at Datong many strong men fled to the northern desert to serve the bandits; now they should be summoned to return.
translations.idiomatic: Datong mutiny refugees serving enemies should be recalled.

sentences.zh: 有攜畜產器械來者，聽其自有。

translations.literal: Those who come bringing livestock and tools should be allowed to keep them.
translations.idiomatic: Returnees may keep livestock and tools.

sentences.zh: 更給牛種費，優復數年。

translations.literal: Further give oxen, seed, and expenses and grant tax relief for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Give seed oxen, funds, and tax relief.

sentences.zh: 則我捐金十萬，可得壯士二萬。

translations.literal: Then for one hundred thousand cash in silver we could obtain twenty thousand strong men.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand taels could buy twenty thousand fighters.

sentences.zh: 拊而用之，皆勁旅也。

translations.literal: Comfort them and use them—all are crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: Win them over and they become crack troops.

sentences.zh: 孰與棄之以資強敵哉！

translations.literal: Who would abandon them to strengthen the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Better than abandoning them to the enemy!

sentences.zh: 大同最敵沖，為鎮巡者較諸邊獨難。

translations.literal: Datong faces the enemy most directly; for the grand coordinator and regional commander it is harder than other frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: Datong is the hardest frontier post.

sentences.zh: 今宜不拘資格，精擇其人。

translations.literal: Now qualifications should not bind selection; choose the finest men.
translations.idiomatic: Choose the finest regardless of seniority.

sentences.zh: 豐給祿廩，使得收召猛士，畜豢健丁。

translations.literal: Richly supply salary and grain so they can gather fierce warriors and raise strong youths.
translations.idiomatic: Pay them well to gather fighters.

sentences.zh: 又久其期，非十年不得代。

translations.literal: Also extend their term so that without ten years they cannot be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-year terms would stop short-term thinking.

sentences.zh: 彼知不可驟遷，必不為茍且旦夕計，而邊圉自固。

translations.literal: Knowing they cannot be quickly transferred, they will not plan for the moment alone, and the frontier will naturally be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Long terms would secure the frontier.

sentences.zh: 又必稍寬文綱，非大幹憲典，言官毋得輕劾，以壞其成功。

translations.literal: Also the literary net must be somewhat relaxed; unless a great breach of law, remonstrance officials should not lightly impeach and ruin success.
translations.idiomatic: Relax petty impeachment of frontier leaders.

sentences.zh: 至用間之道，兵家所貴。

translations.literal: As for using spies, the military arts prize this.
translations.idiomatic: Espionage is militarily vital.

sentences.zh: 今寇諜獲於山西者已數十人，他鎮類是。

translations.literal: Today dozens of bandit spies have been captured in Shanxi alone, and other garrisons are similar.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of enemy spies were caught in Shanxi alone.

sentences.zh: 故我之虛實，彼無不知。

translations.literal: Thus our strengths and weaknesses—they know all.
translations.idiomatic: So enemies know our every weakness.

sentences.zh: 今宜厚養死士，潛縱遣之。

translations.literal: Now dead soldiers should be richly maintained and secretly sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Maintain dead soldiers' families and send agents out.

sentences.zh: 得間則斬其名王、部長及諸用事貴人。

translations.literal: When there is opportunity behead their named kings, chiefs, and powerful nobles in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Kill enemy princes and chiefs when possible.

sentences.zh: 否亦可覘強弱虛實，而陰為備。

translations.literal: Otherwise too one can observe strength and weakness and secretly prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Or spy to learn strength and prepare.

sentences.zh: 又寇貪而好利，我誠不愛金帛。

translations.literal: Moreover bandits are greedy and love profit; we truly should not begrudge gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies love gold; use it freely.

sentences.zh: 東賂黃、毛三衛以牽其左，西收亦不剌遺種，予善地，以綴其右，使首尾掣曳，自相狼顧，則我可起承其敝，坐收全勝矣。

translations.literal: Bribe the Three Guards of Huang and Mao to the east to pull their left wing; to the west win the surviving tribes of Builai, give good land, and slow their right—make them pull fore and aft and look back in mutual fear, then we can rise and take their exhaustion and sit in complete victory.
translations.idiomatic: Bribe eastern and western tribes to divide the enemy, then strike when they fray.

sentences.zh: 他所條析，鹹切邊計。

translations.literal: Other items he analyzed were all apt to frontier planning.
translations.idiomatic: His other points all suited frontier needs.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其忠懇，進秩左參政。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his loyal earnestness and promoted him one rank to left administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and promoted him to left administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 松疏上，當事者已惡其侵官。

translations.literal: When Song's memorial went up, those in charge already hated his encroachment on their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Officials already hated his encroaching advice.

sentences.zh: 及遷擢，益忌之。

translations.literal: When he was promoted and transferred, they hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion made them hate him more.

sentences.zh: 不畀以兵柄，令於三關聽用，欲因以陷之。

translations.literal: They did not give him military authority but ordered him employed at the three passes, intending thereby to trap him.
translations.idiomatic: They denied him command and posted him at three passes to trap him.

sentences.zh: 寇大入，抵太原。

translations.literal: Bandits raided deeply and reached Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders reached Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 給事中馮良知遂劾松建言冒賞，無寸功。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Feng Zhixian then impeached Song for seeking reward by reckless memorializing without the slightest merit.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zhixian charged Song with reckless talk and no merit.

sentences.zh: 紀功科道官張堯年、王珩劾總兵官張達等，並論松虛議無補，遂斥為民。

translations.literal: Merit-recording censors Zhang Yaonian and Wang Hang impeached regional commander Zhang Da and others and also judged Song's empty proposals useless; he was dismissed as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Merit censors joined in; Song was dismissed as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 家居十余年。

translations.literal: At home for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home over ten years.

sentences.zh: 屢薦，輒報罷。

translations.literal: Repeatedly recommended, each time the reply was dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Every recommendation was rejected.

sentences.zh: 至三十五年，以趙文華言，起陜西參政，分守平涼。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, on Zhao Wenhua's word, he was raised as administration commissioner of Shaanxi to defend Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35 Zhao Wenhua had him made Shaanxi commissioner defending Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 復條嚴保甲、均賦稅、置常平、簡伉健數事。

translations.literal: He again listed strict baojia, equal tax assessment, granary reserves, and selecting strong men among other matters.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed baojia, fair taxes, granaries, and strong militia.

sentences.zh: 三遷江西左布政使，以右副都御史巡撫其地。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became left administration commissioner of Jiangxi and right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of that region.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Jiangxi left commissioner and grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 所部多盜，松奏設南昌、南豐、萬安三營，遣將討捕，以次削平。

translations.literal: The area had many bandits; Song memorialized to set three camps at Nanchang, Nanfeng, and Wan'an, sent generals to pursue and capture, and pacified them in order.
translations.idiomatic: He set three camps and pacified Jiangxi bandits in order.

sentences.zh: 進兵部右侍郎，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right vice minister of war while remaining grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: He became right vice war minister while staying coordinator.

sentences.zh: 以會討廣東巨寇張璉及援閩破倭功，兩賜銀幣。

translations.literal: For joining the campaign against Guangdong great bandit Zhang Lian and aiding Fujian to break the Japanese pirates, he twice received gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He twice received gold for crushing Zhang Lian and aiding Fujian against pirates.

sentences.zh: 居三年，召理部事。

translations.literal: After three years he was summoned to manage the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was recalled to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 進左侍郎，改吏部。

translations.literal: He advanced to left vice minister and was moved to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He became left vice minister then personnel vice minister.

sentences.zh: 遷南京兵部尚書，參贊機務。

translations.literal: He was moved to Minister of War at Nanjing to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became Nanjing war minister assisting military affairs.

sentences.zh: 代郭樸為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He replaced Guo Pu as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Guo Pu as personnel minister.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「撫按舉劾，每舉數十人，虛譽浮詞，往往失實。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "When grand coordinators and inspectors recommend and impeach, they often name dozens of men with empty reputation and floating words, often missing the truth."
translations.idiomatic: He said touring officials' bulk recommendations were often false.

sentences.zh: 所劾犯贓，僅擬降調；

translations.literal: Those impeached for corruption are only proposed for demotion and transfer;
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt men were only demoted, not removed;

sentences.zh: 罷軟貪殘，僅擬改教。

translations.literal: the incompetent, corrupt, and cruel are only proposed for transfer to teaching posts.
translations.idiomatic: the incompetent were merely sent to teach.

sentences.zh: 賞罰不當，人何所激勸？

translations.literal: When rewards and punishments are not fitting, how are people to be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: Bad rewards and punishments could not inspire men.

sentences.zh: 且巡撫歲終例有冊，第屬吏賢否，今皆寢閣，乞申飭其欺玩者。

translations.literal: Moreover touring inspectors' year-end registers usually list subordinates' worth, but now all lie idle—I beg that those who deceive be admonished.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to punish inspectors who shelved year-end reviews.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 松潔己好修，富經術，郁然有聲望。

translations.literal: Song was frugal and fond of cultivation, rich in classical learning, and quietly possessed reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Song was learned, frugal, and respected.

sentences.zh: 晚主銓柄，以振拔淹滯為己任。

translations.literal: Late in holding the power of appointment he took raising the long-stalled as his duty.
translations.idiomatic: Late as personnel minister he promoted the long-neglected.

sentences.zh: 甫七月，病卒。

translations.literal: After only seven months he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness after seven months.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚恭肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously junior guardian with the title Gongsu.

sentences.zh: 時又有胡松者，字茂卿，績溪人。

translations.literal: At the same time there was another Hu Song, styled Maoqing, a native of Jixi.
translations.idiomatic: Another Hu Song, courtesy name Maoqing, came from Jixi.

sentences.zh: 正德九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Zhengde 9.

sentences.zh: 嘉請時為御史。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing period he was a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiaqing he was a censor.

sentences.zh: 桂萼薦王瓊，松論之。

translations.literal: When Gui E recommended Wang Qiong, Song argued against it.
translations.idiomatic: He opposed Gui E's recommendation of Wang Qiong.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，謫廉州推官。

translations.literal: Offending the imperial will, he was demoted to investigating prefect of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the throne and was demoted to Lianzhou investigating prefect.

sentences.zh: 累官工部尚書。

translations.literal: After several promotions he became Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 伊王欲拓其洛陽府第，計直十萬金，以十二賕嚴嵩，期必得。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi wished to expand his Luoyang mansion, estimating one hundred thousand cash in value, and gave one hundred twenty bribes to Yan Song, expecting to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yi tried to bribe Yan Song for a costly Luoyang expansion.

sentences.zh: 松據祖制爭，乃止。

translations.literal: Song argued on ancestral institution and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Song blocked it on ancestral precedent.

sentences.zh: 俺答入寇，仇鸞以邊眾入衛，欲悉召其眾實京師，移武庫仗於營，便給調。

translations.literal: When Altan invaded, Qiu Luan brought frontier troops to guard the capital and wished to summon them all to fill the capital, moving arsenal weapons to camps for convenient distribution.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Luan wanted all frontier troops in the capital and arsenal weapons in camps.

sentences.zh: 松言邊兵外也而內之，武庫仗內也而外之，非所以重肘腋，杜微慎防也，執弗許。

translations.literal: Song said frontier troops are external yet would be placed within, and arsenal weapons are internal yet placed without—not the way to weight the armpit and guard against minute dangers—and held firm and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Song refused: frontier troops inside and weapons outside endangered the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋引疾歸。

translations.literal: Soon he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired ill.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十三。

translations.literal: He died aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 居家以孝友稱。

translations.literal: At home he was praised for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: At home he was famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 趙炳然，字子晦，劍州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Bingran, styled Zihui, was a native of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bingran, courtesy name Zihui, came from Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Jiajing 14.

sentences.zh: 除新喻知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Xinyu magistrate.

sentences.zh: 征拜御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as censor.

sentences.zh: 與給事中李文進核宣、大、山西兵餉。

translations.literal: Together with supervising secretary Li Wenjin he audited military funds of Xuan, Dat, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Wenjin he audited Xuan-Dat-Shanxi military funds.

sentences.zh: 劾前後督撫樊繼祖、史道，監司楊銳，指揮馮世彪等一百七十七人侵冒罪，坐謫有差。

translations.literal: He impeached former and later grand coordinators Fan Jizu and Shi Dao, surveillance commissioner Yang Rui, commander Feng Shibiao, and one hundred seventy-seven others for embezzlement; demotions and punishments differed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached 177 officials for fund embezzlement with varied punishments.

sentences.zh: 條上備邊十二事。

translations.literal: He listed twelve frontier defense measures.
translations.idiomatic: He listed twelve frontier defense measures.

sentences.zh: 歷按雲南、浙江。

translations.literal: He toured as inspector in Yunnan and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected Yunnan and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 擢大理寺丞，進少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and advanced to vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: He became judicial review vice director then vice minister.

sentences.zh: 尋改右僉都御史，巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Huguang grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 進左副都御史，協理院事。

translations.literal: He advanced to left vice censor-in-chief and assisted in managing the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He became left vice censor-in-chief assisting the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 浙江、福建總督胡宗憲下獄，詔罷總督毋設。

translations.literal: Zhejiang-Fujian grand coordinator Hu Zongxian was imprisoned; an edict abolished the grand coordinator post.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongxian was jailed and the grand coordinator post abolished.

sentences.zh: 大學士徐階以浙江寇甫平，請設巡撫綏輯，遂進炳然兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史往任之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xu Jie, because Zhejiang bandits had just been pacified, asked to set a grand coordinator to soothe the region, and Bingran was advanced to right vice minister of war and right vice censor-in-chief to take the post.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie asked for a Zhejiang grand coordinator; Bingran was sent.

sentences.zh: 浙罹兵燹久，又當宗憲汰侈後，財匱力絀。

translations.literal: Zhejiang had long suffered from warfare and, after Zongxian's removal for extravagance, funds were depleted and strength exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: War-ravaged Zhejiang was broke after Zongxian's extravagance.

sentences.zh: 炳然廉以率下，悉更諸政令不便者，仍奏減軍需之半。

translations.literal: Bingran led subordinates with integrity, changed all inconvenient policies, and again memorialized to halve military needs—the people all blessed him.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled frugally, reformed policy, halved military levies, and won popular blessing.

sentences.zh: 民皆屍祝之。

translations.literal: The people all blessed him as if to a god.
translations.idiomatic: People blessed him like a god.

sentences.zh: 福建巡撫遊震得請浙兵剿賊。

translations.literal: Fujian grand coordinator You Zhen obtained approval to send Zhejiang troops to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: You Zhen won Zhejiang troops for Fujian bandits.

sentences.zh: 詔發義烏精兵一萬，命副總兵戚繼光將以往，仍諭炳然協剿。

translations.literal: An edict sent ten thousand elite troops from Yiwu, with vice regional commander Qi Jiguang to lead them, still ordering Bingran to coordinate suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand Yiwu troops under Qi Jiguang were sent with Bingran to coordinate.

sentences.zh: 炳然言：「福建所以致亂者，由將吏撫馭無術，民變為兵，兵變為盜耳。

translations.literal: Bingran said: "The reason Fujian fell into chaos is that generals and officials had no skill in control; the people turned into soldiers and soldiers into bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Bingran said Fujian's chaos came from bad civil control turning people into rebels.

sentences.zh: 今又驅浙兵以赴閩急，竊懼浙之復為閩也。

translations.literal: "Now again driving Zhejiang troops to Fujian's emergency, I fear Zhejiang will become like Fujian."
translations.idiomatic: "Sending Zhejiang troops to Fujian may ruin Zhejiang too."

sentences.zh: 請令一意團練士著，使人各為用，家自為守，急則兵，緩則農，然後聚散兩有所歸。

translations.literal: "I ask that training focus wholly on local militia so each man serves and each household defends—in urgency soldiers, in calm farmers—then gathering and dispersing both have a place."
translations.idiomatic: He urged local militia who farm in peace and fight in crisis.

sentences.zh: 即不得已而召募，亦必先本土後鄰壤，庶無釀禍本。

translations.literal: "Even if recruitment is unavoidable, native soil should come before neighboring regions, lest the root of disaster be planted."
translations.idiomatic: If recruiting, hire locals before outsiders.

sentences.zh: 」又條上防海八事，中言：「蘇、松、浙江水師皆統於總兵，駐定海；

translations.literal: " He also listed eight coastal defense measures, among them saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed eight coastal defense measures:

sentences.zh: 陸師皆統於副總兵，駐金山衛，並受總督節制。

translations.literal: "Suzhou, Song, and Zhejiang naval forces are all under the regional commander, stationed at Dinghai;
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou-Song-Zhejiang fleets answered to the regional commander at Dinghai;

sentences.zh: 今督府既革，則已判為二鎮，彼此牽制，不得調發。

translations.literal: land forces are under the vice regional commander at Jinshan Guard, all under the grand coordinator's command.
translations.idiomatic: land forces under the vice commander at Jinshan—all under the grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 請畫地分轄，各兼水陸軍務。

translations.literal: "Now that the coordinator's office is gone, they are already two commands, each restraining the other and unable to deploy together."
translations.idiomatic: "Without a coordinator the two commands cannot coordinate."

sentences.zh: 」俱報可。

translations.literal: "I ask that territories be divided for separate jurisdiction, each combining land and naval duties."
translations.idiomatic: "Divide territory so each commander handles land and sea."

sentences.zh: 其年，繼光破賊，瀕海余寇流入浙江。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 官軍迎戰於連嶼、陡橋、石坪，斬首百余級。

translations.literal: That year Jiguang defeated bandits; coastal remnant bandits flowed into Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiguang won; remnant raiders fled into Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 新倭復犯石坪，將士乘勝殲之。

translations.literal: Government troops met them at Lianyu, Douqiao, and Shiping and beheaded more than one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Troops took 100+ heads at Lianyu, Douqiao, and Shiping.

sentences.zh: 炳然以援剿功，再賜金幣，進右都御史兼兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: New Japanese raiders again attacked Shiping; officers and soldiers destroyed them riding the victory.
translations.idiomatic: New raiders at Shiping were destroyed in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 給事中辛自修劾罷戎政都御史李鐩，請擇素知兵者代之。

translations.literal: Bingran, for merit in aiding suppression, again received gold and silks and was promoted to right censor-in-chief and right vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: For aid in suppression he was promoted and rewarded again.

sentences.zh: 乃召炳然為兵部尚書，協理戎政。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Xin Zixiu impeached and dismissed Military Administration Censor-in-Chief Li Jin and asked that someone who truly knew warfare replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zixiu removed Li Jin and sought a military expert.

sentences.zh: 逾年，詔兼右都御史，總督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: Bingran was then summoned as Minister of War and assisted in military administration.
translations.idiomatic: Bingran was summoned as war minister assisting military administration.

sentences.zh: 新平、平遠、保平三堡密邇宣府，舊屬大同。

translations.literal: A year later an edict also made him right censor-in-chief and director-general of military affairs in Xuan, Dat, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he also directed Xuan-Dat-Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 天城相去六十里，孤懸塞外，隔崇山，寇騎時出沒。

translations.literal: The three forts Xinping, Pingyuan, and Baoping lie close to Xuanfu and formerly belonged to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Forts Xinping, Pingyuan, and Baoping near Xuanfu once belonged to Datong.

sentences.zh: 炳然奏添設參將，別為一營，報可。

translations.literal: Tiancheng was sixty li away, isolated beyond the pass, separated by high mountains, and bandit horsemen often appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Tiancheng stood isolated beyond the pass where raiders roamed.

sentences.zh: 尋以總兵官馬芳等卻敵功，被賚。

translations.literal: Bingran memorialized to add a regional vice commander and separate camp; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He added a vice commander and separate camp.

sentences.zh: 已，召還部，代楊博為尚書。

translations.literal: Soon for regional commander Ma Fang and others' merit in repelling the enemy he was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Fang's repulse brought him rewards.

sentences.zh: 考滿，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled to the ministry and replaced Yang Bo as minister.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he replaced Yang Bo as minister.

sentences.zh: 炳然清勤練達，所至有聲績。

translations.literal: When his term review was complete he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At term review he was made junior guardian.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，以病乞休去。

translations.literal: Bingran was pure, diligent, and experienced; wherever he went he had reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Bingran was pure, capable, and effective everywhere.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保，謚恭襄。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing, on grounds of illness he asked to retire and left.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing he retired ill.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：世宗朝，璁、萼、言、嵩相繼用事，六卿之長不得其職。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Gongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously grand guardian with the title Gongxiang.

sentences.zh: 大都波流茅靡，淟，忍取容。

translations.literal: The comment says: In Shizong's court Cong, E, Yan, and Song succeeded one another in power; the heads of the six ministries could not perform their duties.
translations.idiomatic: The comment: under Shizong, Cong, E, Yan, and Song seized power and six ministers lost their roles.

sentences.zh: 廖紀以下諸人，其矯矯者與！

translations.literal: Most drifted with the current, obsequious and enduring to find favor.
translations.idiomatic: Most officials drifted, obsequious and compliant.

sentences.zh: 應奎司邦計，不能節以制度，顧務加賦以病民。

translations.literal: Among Liao Ji and the men below, were they not the outstanding ones!
translations.idiomatic: Liao Ji and those below stood out.

sentences.zh: 豹也碌碌，彌無足觀矣。

translations.literal: Yingkui held state accounts yet could not restrain by institutions and instead added levies to afflict the people. Bao was mediocre and even less worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui taxed without institutions; Bao was mediocre and negligible.
